# Overview: design invariants and notation (LR 1, LR 2)

<!-- covers: LR 1, LR 2 -->
*Agent mode. Human mode: [A tour of Fortis](../guide/tour.md). Source of truth: LR 1 and LR 2.*

LR 1 and LR 2 state no numbered rules; they fix the invariants every later rule serves. Write code so that each of
these is visible on the line.

## Invariants

| Invariant | Consequence when writing code | LR |
|---|---|---|
| Every local decision is visible: ownership operations, mutation permission, failure disposition, effect claims, observation points. | Never rely on inference for these; write the marker, modifier or handler. A marker the declaration already shows is left out: an `editable self` call on a `let mut` binding, `return local` (LR 7.5). | LR 1 |
| Imported signatures can never be weaker than their bodies. | Read the callee's signature (`fortis view --symbol`) instead of its body. | LR 1 |
| Library-first: program = packages, package = modules, module = one file; HTTP, data, web UI, telemetry, jobs are kits (libraries). | The core imports nothing from kits. | LR 1 |
| Explicit ownership: assigning or passing an existing owned value states `copy`, `alias` or `move`; mutable access is `editable`. No hidden clones or reference counts. | See [ownership](07-ownership.md). | LR 1 |
| Three distinct answers: `T?`, `Bool`, `Outcome[T]` with `??`, `\|\|`, `or`. Nothing is truthy. | Compare explicitly (`x != null`, `n != 0`). | LR 1 |
| Linear failures: an outcome is consumed exactly once (`or fail`, `or recover`, `catch`, `match`, `report`); dropping one is a compile error. | Every call to a `try` function is followed by a disposition; in a `test` or `property` body `or fail` is implied (LR 14). | LR 1 |
| Closed effect set: `pure`, `noalloc`, `async`, `try` are checked claims over eight effects; contracts are conjunctions of them. | See [effects](11-effects.md). | LR 1 |
| Lexical loans; synchronous `defer`; one cancellation point (`await`); structured `scope`. | End a loan early by closing a block. | LR 1 |
| Two backends, one semantics: development VM and safe-Rust native code run the same checked IR. | Never depend on backend behaviour. | LR 1 |
| Absent by design: scripting semantics, runtime reflection, inheritance, macros, exceptions, implicit conversions. | Do not emulate them. | LR 1 |

## Notation

Every non-alphabetic symbol and what it answers (LR 1.1):

| Notation | Meaning | Never |
|---|---|---|
| `{ }` | block, record literal, record type | |
| `( )` | call, parameter list, tuple, grouping | |
| `Name[ ]` | generic arguments after an uppercase name | |
| `place[ ]` | index after a lowercase place | slices |
| `fn[ ]` | a lambda's capture list, only when non-empty | `fn[]` |
| `+ - * / %` `<< >>` `& \| ^` | arithmetic and bitwise; proof-required on integers | overloading |
| `== !=` `< <= > >=` | `Equatable`, `Comparable`; IEEE comparison on floats | chained comparisons |
| `&& \|\|` `!` | Boolean logic | truthiness |
| `+=` and friends | `x = x op e` | |
| `< >` after a type | refinement (type position only) | |
| `:` | has type, named argument, record field, label | ternary, slicing |
| `=` | assignment, `let` initialiser | equality |
| `=>` | expression body of a function, lambda or match arm | map literals |
| `.` | member access, module paths | ranges |
| `..` `..<` | integer ranges in `for` headers and refinements | |
| `?` `?.` | optional type suffix, optional chaining | error propagation |
| `??` | absent-value fallback | |
| `@name(args)` | apply an aspect, on the lines above a function head | contracts |
| `${ }` | string interpolation | |
| `//` | comment; documentation directly above a declaration | `///`, `/* */` |
| `,` | list separator | |
| `...` | spread a place into a constructor; forward remaining aspect arguments | |

Keywords that carry a decision (LR 1.1): `let` (new name), `mut` (changes), `copy`/`alias`/`move`/`editable`
(how a place is used), `owned`/`editable` on a parameter, `try`/`pure`/`noalloc`/`async`/`recovers` and named
contracts in the modifier position, `or fail`/`or recover`/`catch`, `give`, `export`.

Silence (LR 1.1): an unmarked argument, or the receiver of a `self` method, is a read loan ending when the call
returns (or with the future of an `async` call); an unmarked `for` source is a read loan for the loop; an unmarked
assignment is a fresh or trivial value. The unmarked receiver of an `editable self` method, or a `fn mut` being
called, is the exclusive loan its root's declaration shows (`let mut`, `editable`), and `return local` moves the
local (LR 7.5).

Removed, never write (LR 1.1): semicolons; `///`, `/* */`; `yield`; `or die`; `nostate`; `self: editable Self`
(write `editable self`); `alias editable` (write `editable`); `alias type` (a `type` is always nominal); `within`;
`give` in a single-expression arm; `fn[]`; `::`; operator overloading; implicit `it`; postfix `?` for errors; `new`
(name constructors `create`, `of`, `from`); `return` in an expression-bodied function.

Two deliberate costs (LR 1.1): `(f() or fail).amount` needs parentheses, so write `let v = f() or fail` on its own
line; an `async` call builds a `Future`, and `await` or `launch` is the visible point where it runs.

Formatted source shows every inferred fact (closure kind, loan modes, a contract's modifiers), except a lambda's
inferred `pure`/`noalloc`, which the function type it is passed to states (LR 1.1, LR 8.2). `fortis fmt --write`
also rewrites older forms into the forms these pages teach where the meaning is unchanged; run it before review.

## Correction patterns: notation from other languages

All of these are `E-SYN-000` (LR 3.2), a sentence outside the grammar of LR 1.1's notation.

### Postfix `?` for errors (LR 1.1)

```fortis
// reject: E-SYN-000
try func parse(n: Int) Int => n

try func twice(n: Int) Int {
  let v = parse(n)?                   // reject: E-SYN-000
  return v
}

test "twice" {
  expect twice(2) == 2
}
```

```fortis
// accept
try func parse(n: Int) Int => n

try func twice(n: Int) Int {
  let v = parse(n) or fail
  return v
}

test "twice" {
  expect twice(2) == 2
}
```

### Empty capture list (LR 1.1)

```fortis
// reject: E-SYN-000
pure func countPositive(items: List[Int]) Int {
  let positive = fn[](n: Int) Bool => n > 0    // reject: E-SYN-000
  return items.countWhere(positive)
}

test "countPositive" {
  expect countPositive(List.of(1, -2, 3)) == 2
}
```

```fortis
// accept
pure func countPositive(items: List[Int]) Int {
  let positive = pure noalloc fn(n: Int) Bool => n > 0
  return items.countWhere(positive)
}

test "countPositive" {
  expect countPositive(List.of(1, -2, 3)) == 2
}
```

### `return` in an expression body (LR 1.1)

```fortis
// reject: E-SYN-000
pure func double(n: Int<0..100>) Int => return n * 2    // reject: E-SYN-000

test "double" {
  expect double(2) == 4
}
```

```fortis
// accept
pure func double(n: Int<0..100>) Int => n * 2

test "double" {
  expect double(2) == 4
}
```

### `::` paths and `new` (LR 1.1)

```fortis
// reject: E-SYN-000
class Point {
  export x: Int
}

pure func origin() Point => Point::new(0)     // reject: E-SYN-000

test "origin" {
  expect origin().x == 0
}
```

```fortis
// accept
class Point {
  export x: Int
  export pure func of(x: Int) Point => Point(x)
}

pure func origin() Point => Point.of(0)

test "origin" {
  expect origin().x == 0
}
```

## The worked module (LR 2)

LR 2 is one module that uses every construct; [the tour](../guide/tour.md) has a self-contained counterpart that
runs. Its constructs, by section:

| Construct in LR 2 | Example | LR |
|---|---|---|
| imports: aliased module, braced members | `import fortis.text`, `import fortis.money { Money, Currency }` | LR 4.3 |
| nominal refined newtype | `export type CustomerId = Int<1..>` | LR 6.9, LR 6.3 |
| class with exported and private fields, generated constructor | `export class Line derive Equatable { … }` | LR 9.1, LR 9.2 |
| refined field type | `quantity: Int<1..10000>` | LR 6.3 |
| method modes | `total(self)`, `issue(editable self, …)` | LR 9.3, LR 7.6 |
| enum with payloads | `Issued(at: Timestamp)` | LR 9.7 |
| declared failure with payload and template | `export error CurrencyMismatch { … }` | LR 10.3 |
| interface, mixin with `requires` | `Renderable`, `Summarised` | LR 9.5, LR 9.6 |
| fallible associated constructor | `pure try func create(…) Invoice` with `fail` | LR 9.2, LR 10.1 |
| `or fail` propagation, return of a local (a move) | `let lineTotal = line.total() or fail`, `return sum` | LR 10.2, LR 7.5 |
| `editable self` call on a `let mut` binding, unmarked | `out.appendLine(…)` | LR 7.5 |
| exhaustive `match` with payload bindings | `Paid(at: paidAt, reference: ref) => …` | LR 9.8 |
| closure with explicit kind and capture | `pure fn[alias threshold](line: Line) Bool { … }` | LR 8.2, LR 8.3 |
| `defer`, `catch` with `report` and `recover`, `recovers` | `withAudit` | LR 12.1, LR 10.4 |
| tests, table test with `as row` | `test "quantity boundary" cases { … } as row { … }` | LR 14 |
| entry point in another package, capabilities as parameters | `try func main(console: Console)` | LR 4.6 |

---
source: docs/agent/03-lexical.md
---

# Lexical structure (LR 3)

<!-- covers: LR 3 -->
*Agent mode. Human mode: [Lexical structure](../guide/03-lexical.md). Source of truth: LR 3.*

## Rules

| Rule | Statement | LR |
|---|---|---|
| LANG-03-01 | A `;` outside strings, comments and raw template regions is a parse error (`E-SYN-001`). There is no semicolon token and no automatic insertion. | LR 3.2 |
| LANG-03-02 | A newline ends a statement unless (a) it is inside `(…)`, `[…]` or `{…}` of the same expression or argument list, (b) the line ends with a trailing continuation token, or (c) the next line starts with a leading continuation token. Refinement `<` `>` are not continuation tokens. | LR 3.2 |
| LANG-03-03 | Uppercase first letter: type, interface, mixin, enum, variant, contract, error kind, observation schema. Lowercase or `_`: value, function, method, field, parameter, module alias, label. Decided lexically, no symbol table. | LR 3.3 |
| LANG-03-04 | Every keyword of LR Appendix A is reserved in every declaration and binding position (`E-SYN-002`), including the kit heads; a keyword is a valid name after `.` and as a method or associated-function name. | LR 3.4 |
| LANG-03-05 | Literal typing follows the LR 3.5 table; an out-of-range literal is rejected at compile time (`E-REF-001`). | LR 3.5 |
| LANG-03-06 | Each interpolated expression is evaluated once, left to right, must be `Displayable`, and must not be fallible or suspending. | LR 3.6 |

## Token facts

| Fact | LR |
|---|---|
| Source: UTF-8, extension `.ft`; identifiers ASCII `[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*`; Unicode only in strings, comments and data; a byte-order mark is rejected. | LR 3.1 |
| Quotas: a file over 16 MiB or 2,000,000 tokens, or nesting of brackets, blocks, prefix operators or interpolations deeper than 256, is `E-LIM-002` and is not parsed. | LR 3.1 |
| Trailing continuation tokens: `,` `(` `[` `=` `=>` `+` `-` `*` `/` `%` `<<` `>>` `&` `\|` `^` `&&` `\|\|` `??` `==` `!=` `<` `<=` `>` `>=` `..` `..<` `.` | LR 3.2 |
| Leading continuation tokens: `.` `or` `catch` `??` `else` `)` `]` `with` `where` `implements` `derive` `from` | LR 3.2 |
| Body brace (statement block or declaration body) vs expression brace (record literal or type): decided by the token before `{`; expression brace after `=`, `(`, `,`, `:`, `[`, `??`, `==`, `!=`, a compound assignment, `return`, `give`, `fail`, `recover`. A body may be one line: `{ statement }`. | LR 3.2 |
| `return`, `fail`, `give` take their operand on the same line; a bare `return` on its own line returns `Void`. | LR 3.2 |
| Parsing decisions P1 (one `NL` per run of blank/comment lines), P2 (longest chains), P3 (alternatives in grammar order) are normative for any parser. | LR 3.2 |
| Integer literal: decimal, `0x`, `0b`, `0o`, `_` separators; type from context, default `Int`. Float: needs `.` or exponent; `f32` suffix gives `Float32`. Decimal: `d` suffix. Duration: `ms` `s` `min` `h`. | LR 3.5 |
| `"text"` is `StringView from static`; `"a ${x}"` is a fresh `String` that a binding annotated `StringView` cannot hold (`E-TYP-040`); `"""raw"""` is `StringView from static`, no escapes, no interpolation; `b"abc"` is `BytesView from static`; `null` is the absent case of `T?`. | LR 3.5 |
| Interpolation takes a read loan of the places it names; it never escapes for HTML or any other context. | LR 3.6 |
| Comments: only `//`. Documentation is the `//` run directly above a declaration with no blank line between. A fenced `fortis` block in documentation needs a first-line marker (`// accept`, `// reject: CODE`, `// execute: R`, `// illustrative`). | LR 3.7 |

## Diagnostics

| Code | Trigger | Correction | LR |
|---|---|---|---|
| E-SYN-001 | `;` in code | delete it (the record carries the edit) | LR 3.2 |
| E-SYN-000 | not a sentence of the grammar: a line starting with a binary operator, `/* */`, a byte-order mark, a top-level statement | move the operator to the end of the previous line; use `//`; remove the mark | LR 3.2 |
| E-SYN-002 | keyword used as a declaration, binding or parameter name (`match`, `state`, `view`, `model`, …) | rename; keywords are valid only after `.` and as method or associated-function names | LR 3.4 |
| E-REF-001 | literal outside its target type or refinement | change the literal or widen the declared type | LR 3.5 |
| E-TYP-040 | interpolated expression not `Displayable` (including an `Outcome` from a fallible call); interpolated literal bound to a `StringView` | bind the result first (`let v = f() or fail`, then `${v}`); annotate `String` | LR 3.5 |
| E-LIM-002 | source over the size, token or nesting quota | split the file or reduce nesting | LR 3.1 |

## Correction patterns

### E-SYN-001: semicolon (LR 3.2)

The record carries a correction, an edit that deletes the semicolon; apply it as given.

```fortis
// reject: E-SYN-001
pure func pair() Int {
  let a = 1; let b = 2           // reject: E-SYN-001
  return a + b
}

test "pair" {
  expect pair() == 3
}
```

```output
example.ft:3:12: error E-SYN-001 [LANG-03-01] (Syntax, violated): ';' is not a token
    expected_tokens: []
    found_token: ";"
    correction: delete the semicolon
      example.ft:3:12-3:13 -> ""
```

```fortis
// accept
pure func pair() Int {
  let a = 1
  let b = 2
  return a + b
}

test "pair" {
  expect pair() == 3
}
```

### E-SYN-000: binary operator at the start of a line (LR 3.2)

Binary operators continue a line only when they are last on it.

```fortis
// reject: E-SYN-000
pure func total(a: Int<0..100>, b: Int<0..100>) Int {
  let sum = a
    + b                          // reject: E-SYN-000
  return sum
}

test "total" {
  expect total(1, 2) == 3
}
```

```fortis
// accept
pure func total(a: Int<0..100>, b: Int<0..100>) Int {
  let sum = a +
    b
  return sum
}

test "total" {
  expect total(1, 2) == 3
}
```

Leading `.`, `or`, `catch`, `??` and `else` do continue a line:

```fortis
// accept
pure try func half(n: Int) Int {
  if n % 2 != 0 { return 0 }
  return Int.div(n, 2) or fail
}

pure recovers func pipeline(fallback: Int?) Int {
  let n = fallback
    ?? 7
  let h = half(n)
    or recover -1
  return h
}

test "pipeline" {
  expect pipeline(null) == 0
  expect pipeline(10) == 5
}
```

### E-SYN-002: keyword as a name (LR 3.4)

Kit head words (`state`, `view`, `model`, `component`, `context`, `action`, `resource`, `inject`, `provide`, …)
are reserved like every other keyword.

```fortis
// reject: E-SYN-002
pure func size(state: Int) Int => state     // reject: E-SYN-002

test "size" {
  expect size(1) == 1
}
```

```records
{"class": "Syntax", "code": "E-SYN-002", "column": 16, "fields": {"expected_tokens": ["lowerIdent"], "found_token": "state"}, "file": "example.ft", "line": 2, "message": "keyword 'state' used as an identifier", "rule": "LANG-03-04", "severity": "error", "status": "violated"}
```

```fortis
// accept
pure func size(current: Int) Int => current

test "size" {
  expect size(1) == 1
}
```

A keyword is allowed as a method or associated-function name and after `.`:

```fortis
// accept
class Celsius {
  export degrees: Int
  export pure func from(degrees: Int) Celsius => Celsius(degrees)
}

test "from" {
  expect Celsius.from(21).degrees == 21
}
```

### E-REF-001: literal out of range (LR 3.5)

```fortis
// reject: E-REF-001
pure func percent() Int<0..100> {
  let p: Int<0..100> = 101       // reject: E-REF-001
  return 100
}

test "percent" {
  expect percent() == 101
}
```

```fortis
// accept
pure func percent() Int<0..100> {
  let p: Int<0..100> = 100
  return p
}

test "percent" {
  expect percent() == 100
}
```

### E-TYP-040: interpolation (LR 3.5, LR 3.6)

```fortis
// reject: E-TYP-040
try func risky(n: Int) Int => n

try func label(n: Int) String {
  return "value ${risky(n)}"     // reject: E-TYP-040
}

test "label" {
  expect label(2) == "value 2"
}
```

```fortis
// accept
try func risky(n: Int) Int => n

try func label(n: Int) String {
  let v = risky(n) or fail
  return "value ${v}"
}

test "label" {
  expect label(2) == "value 2"
}
```

```fortis
// reject: E-TYP-040
pure func greeting(name: StringView) Int {
  let text: StringView = "hello, ${name}"     // reject: E-TYP-040
  return text.byteCount()
}

test "greeting" {
  expect greeting("ada") == 10
}
```

```fortis
// accept
pure func greeting(name: StringView) Int {
  let text: String = "hello, ${name}"
  return text.byteCount()
}

test "greeting" {
  expect greeting("ada") == 10
}
```

## Facts used when writing code

- Order: interpolated expressions run once each, left to right with the string (LR 3.6).
- A string literal is free (`StringView from static`); converting it to `String` where a `String` is expected
  allocates and is the one implicit conversion (LR 6.6).
- A byte string literal `b"…"` is a `BytesView from static`; read bytes with `get(index) Byte?` and
  `byteCount()` (LR 3.5, LR 6.6).
- Documentation comments are `//` runs directly above a declaration; `fortis view --decls` lists them (LR 3.7).

---
source: docs/agent/04-modules.md
---

# Modules and packages (LR 4)

<!-- covers: LR 4 -->
*Agent mode. Human mode: [Modules and packages](../guide/04-modules.md). Source of truth: LR 4.*

> Preview: dependencies and lock files (LR 4.1) arrive in v0.2. An async entry point (LR 4.6, LR 12.3) arrives in v0.3. One package, its modules, imports, visibility and the ordinary entry point (LR 4.1, 4.2, 4.3, 4.4, 4.5 and 4.6) are in v0.0.1.

## Rules

| Rule | Statement | LR |
|---|---|---|
| LANG-04-01 | A module is one file under `src/`; its path is its identity (`src/a/b.ft` is `a.b`, imported from another package as `PKG.a.b`). A module holds only declarations and `const` bindings with compile-time constant initialisers. | LR 4.2 |
| LANG-04-02 | Importing a module executes no code (there is no module initialisation). | LR 4.2 |
| LANG-04-03 | Across packages, only modules listed in the exporting package's `exports:` may be imported. | LR 4.3 |
| LANG-04-04 | Two versions of one package are two packages; a type's identity is its name, package, version and declaring module, so same-named types of two modules or versions never interchange. | LR 4.1 |
| LANG-04-05 | A `let` may not shadow a visible binding (`E-NAM-003`). | LR 4.5 |
| LANG-04-06 | The entry point is the `main` of the manifest's `entry` module, exported or not, with one of the four heads of LR 4.6, each optionally `recovers` (X-155; refused in packages today, D-52); each parameter is `List[String]` or a capability type, each type once (`E-NAM-005`, `E-NAM-006`), supplied by the runtime by its type (X-345). | LR 4.6 |

## Package and import facts

| Fact | LR |
|---|---|
| Package = directory with `project.yaml`, lockfile `fortis.lock`, `src/`. Manifest keys: `schema: fortis.project/v1`, `name`, `version`, `exports: [modules]`, `dependencies: {name: "version"}`, optional `entry: module` (application), optional `root: module`. | LR 4.1 |
| A standard dependency (`fortis`, `fortis.…`) names a package of the compatibility set (`library/fortis/compatibility.yaml`) at the set's version, else `E-NAM-031`. | LR 4.1 |
| Lockfile: when present, resolution uses only it and fetches nothing. Unpinned dependency, unused pin or unreadable lockfile: `E-NAM-020`. Digest mismatch (package, compiler, standard library, Rust toolchain): `E-NAM-021`. `fortis check` verifies package, compiler and standard-library pins; a native build also verifies the Rust toolchain. | LR 4.1 |
| `--target T`: an import of a standard module the target's feature set lacks is `E-NAM-030`, before any native step. A package shipping a Cargo build script is refused by a native build: `E-NAM-032`. | LR 4.1 |
| Limits: manifest over 1 MiB or 10,000 lines `E-LIM-003`; lockfile over 8 MiB or 100,000 lines `E-LIM-004`; toolchain JSON over 256 MiB or nested over 128 `E-LIM-005`. Toolchain failures are records, never crashes: `E-INT-001` (checker defect, with a minimised `reproduction`), `E-INT-002` (generated Rust does not compile), `E-INT-003` (a native tool missing or failing). | LR 4.1 |
| Import forms: `import p.m` binds alias `m`; `import p.m as x` binds `x`; `import p.m { A, b }` binds exactly the listed members. Imports only at the top of a module, before any declaration. | LR 4.3 |
| Path split: the longest prefix naming the current package or a declared dependency is the package; the rest is the module path. Sibling modules therefore import each other by the full path (`import guide.shop.orders`). No matching prefix: an error naming the undeclared package. Ambiguous splits across the dependency set: `E-NAM-010`. | LR 4.3 |
| `root: m` in the manifest makes `import p { … }` mean module `m` of `p`; without it an empty module path is an error. | LR 4.3 |
| `fortis.prelude` is imported implicitly (core types, optional operators, built-in interfaces); `fortis.text`, `fortis.collections`, `fortis.numeric`, `fortis.time`, `fortis.money`, `fortis.host` need imports. Every kit package is named `fortis.<kit>`. | LR 4.3 |
| Importing one name twice, or a name that collides with a local declaration, is an error. Unused import: warning at the baseline lint level, error at the strict one. | LR 4.3 |
| `export` is the only visibility modifier. Unexported: private to the module. Exported: visible to importers; outside the package only if the module is in `exports:`. Class fields, methods, associated functions: private unless `export`. Enum variants, interface members and mixin-required methods share their declaration's visibility. | LR 4.4 |
| Generated constructor `C(field: …)` is callable only where every field is visible. An exported field is readable through any loan and writable through an `editable` one. | LR 4.4 |
| Names resolve to the innermost enclosing block, then the module namespace. Qualified forms: `module.member`, `Type.associated`, `Enum.Variant`, `value.field`, `value.method(…)`. No `::`. A bare field name is not in scope inside a method: use `self.field`. | LR 4.5 |
| `func main(console: Console, args: List[String])` with modifiers `try`, `async` or `async try`; the result is `Void`, left out; `export` is implied. Each parameter is supplied by its type: `List[String]` gets the arguments, a capability type imported from `fortis.host` gets that capability; declare only what the body uses (`func main()` takes nothing). `main` owns its capabilities and may move one (`Shared.create(move console)`). Older code writes `export func main(args: List[String]) Void` and calls `Host.capabilities()` once in the body; that stays accepted in a `main` with no capability parameter, and `fortis fmt` rewrites it. A failing `try main` prints one failure record to standard error and exits 1. An `async main` is the root task on the core cooperative executor. | LR 4.6 |

## Diagnostics

| Code | Trigger | Correction | LR |
|---|---|---|---|
| E-NAM-003 | `let` shadows a visible binding | rename | LR 4.5 |
| E-NAM-004 | use of a declaration or member not visible at the use site | `export` it (and list its module in `exports:` for other packages), or use an exported API | LR 4.4 |
| E-TYP-030 | exported signature (function, method, field, constant) names a non-exported type | `export` the type, or keep the function private | LR 4.4 |
| E-NAM-010 | dependency set with names that make an import's package/module split ambiguous | rename or drop a dependency | LR 4.3 |
| E-NAM-020, E-NAM-021 | lockfile does not pin the manifests' dependencies, or a digest differs | `fortis lock` after reviewing the change | LR 4.1 |
| E-NAM-030 | import of a standard module the `--target` feature set lacks | remove the import or choose a target that has it | LR 4.1 |
| E-NAM-031 | standard dependency outside the compatibility set or at another version | use the set's version | LR 4.1 |
| E-NAM-032 | package ships a Cargo build script (native build) | remove the build script | LR 4.1 |
| E-LIM-003, E-LIM-004, E-LIM-005 | manifest, lockfile or toolchain JSON over its limit | reduce it | LR 4.1 |
| E-INT-001, E-INT-002, E-INT-003 | toolchain defect, generated Rust rejected, native tool missing | report it with the record's reproduction; not a source error | LR 4.1 |

LR 4.3 and 4.6 state some rules without naming a code: an import of an undeclared package or of a module the
exporting package does not list, an import that collides with a local declaration, and a missing or wrongly typed
`main` are rejected, but which code reports each is not yet settled (X-152). Read the record's `message` and
`fields.candidates` rather than relying on its code.

## Correction patterns

### A package (LR 4.2, LR 4.3)

```yaml
# file: agent.shop/project.yaml
schema: fortis.project/v1
name: agent.shop
version: 1.0.0
entry: main
exports: [prices]
dependencies:
  fortis: "1.0"
```

```fortis
// accept
// file: agent.shop/src/prices.ft
export pure func gross(net: Int<0..1000>) Int => net + net / 5

pure func margin() Int => 3

test "gross adds a fifth" {
  expect gross(100) == 120
}
```

```fortis
// accept
// file: agent.shop/src/main.ft
import fortis.host { Console }
import agent.shop.prices

func main(console: Console) {
  console.print("${prices.gross(100)}")
}
```

```output
120
```

### E-NAM-004: private member of another module (LR 4.4)

```yaml
# file: agent.till/project.yaml
schema: fortis.project/v1
name: agent.till
version: 1.0.0
exports: [prices]
dependencies:
  fortis: "1.0"
```

```fortis
// accept
// file: agent.till/src/prices.ft
export pure func gross(net: Int<0..1000>) Int => net + net / 5

pure func margin() Int => 3

test "gross adds a fifth" {
  expect gross(100) == 120
}
```

`agent.till` is a library. A package that another package depends on is a library: it has no `entry` and no `main`. Only the root program's entry `main` creates the capabilities, and a library's functions receive them as parameters (LR 11.6).

```yaml
# file: agent.tillmix/project.yaml
schema: fortis.project/v1
name: agent.tillmix
version: 1.0.0
entry: main
exports: []
dependencies:
  fortis: "1.0"
  agent.till: "1.0.0"
```

```fortis
// reject: E-NAM-004
// file: agent.tillmix/src/main.ft
import fortis.host { Console }
import agent.till.prices

func main(console: Console) {
  console.print("${prices.gross(100)}")
  discard prices.margin()               // reject: E-NAM-004
}
```

Correction: write `export pure func margin() Int => 3` in `prices`, or stop using it.

### E-TYP-030: exported signature names a private type (LR 4.4)

```fortis
// reject: E-TYP-030
class Hidden {
  export n: Int
}

export pure func make() Hidden => Hidden(n: 1)    // reject: E-TYP-030

test "make" {
  expect make().n == 1
}
```

```fortis
// accept
export class Shown {
  export n: Int
}

export pure func make() Shown => Shown(n: 1)

test "make" {
  expect make().n == 1
}
```

### Import placement and collisions (LR 4.3)

```fortis
// reject: E-SYN-000
pure func one() Int => 1

import fortis.text                // reject: E-SYN-000

test "one" {
  expect one() == 1
}
```

An imported name may not collide with a declaration of the module (`import fortis.money { Money }` beside a local
`class Money` is rejected); the LR names no code for it yet (X-152). Rename the local declaration:

```fortis
// accept
import fortis.money { Money, Currency }

class Price {
  export pennies: Int
}

test "money" {
  expect Price(pennies: 1).pennies == 1
  expect Money.zero(GBP).currency == GBP
}
```

### Entry point (LR 4.6)

`main` declares the capabilities it needs as parameters; the runtime supplies each by its type (X-345).

```fortis
// accept
import fortis.host { Console }

func main(console: Console, args: List[String]) {
  console.print("${args.count()} arguments")
}
```

```output
0 arguments
```

A failing `try main` exits with status 1 and one failure record on standard error; standard output keeps what was
printed before the failure.

```fortis
// accept (exit status 1)
import fortis.host { Path, Console, FileSystem }

try func main(console: Console, fileSystem: FileSystem) {
  console.print("start")
  let text = fileSystem.readText(Path.parse("missing.txt") or fail) or fail
  console.print(text)
}
```

```output
start
```

## Facts used when writing code

- No module initialisation: a module-level value is a `const` with a constant initialiser (LR 4.2, LR 5.1).
- Within a package, imports may be cyclic for type declarations (LR 4.2).
- Renaming an exported declaration or parameter, or moving a module out of `exports:`, breaks other packages
  (LR 4.4, LR 5.8).
- Reach the process's authority only through `main`'s capability parameters, and pass capabilities down as
  parameters (LR 4.6, LR 11.6).

---
source: docs/agent/05-statements.md
---

# Statements and expressions (LR 5)

<!-- covers: LR 5 -->
*Agent mode. Human mode: [Statements and expressions](../guide/05-statements.md). Source of truth: LR 5.*

## Rules

| Rule | Statement | LR |
|---|---|---|
| LANG-05-01 | `let x = e` / `let mut x = e` declare (initialiser required); `let Pattern = move p` destructures a class, tuple or record, and a pattern that can fail to match (a variant, a literal, `null`, `present(…)`, at any depth) is `E-MAT-004`: use `match`; `x = e` assigns only to a visible `let mut` binding, or a field path rooted in a `let mut` binding, an `editable` parameter or an `editable` loan. Assignment is a statement and does not chain. | LR 5.1 |
| LANG-05-02 | Every block exit (fall-through, `return`, `fail`, `break`, `continue`, `give`) ends the block's loans, runs its `defer`s LIFO, then drops its owned locals in reverse initialisation order. | LR 5.1 |
| LANG-05-03 | `if` and `while` conditions are `Bool`; nothing else converts. | LR 5.2 |
| LANG-05-04 | `for i in a..<b` (or `a..b`) gives an immutable index refined to the range; the index is never assignable. | LR 5.3 |
| LANG-05-05 | A non-`Void` function ends every path in `return`, `fail` or a `Never` call; no implicit value. | LR 5.4 |
| LANG-05-06 | Precedence and associativity follow the LR 5.6 table; outcome operators (`or fail`, `or recover`, `catch`), `??` and `&&`/`\|\|` do not mix without parentheses. | LR 5.6 |
| LANG-05-07 | Operands and arguments evaluate left to right, once; receiver before arguments; calls run evaluate, activate, invoke, release. | LR 5.7 |
| LANG-05-08 | A non-`Void` expression statement needs `discard`, except a call of a function declared `@ignorable`; a linear value (`Outcome`, `Future`, `Task`, …) cannot be discarded, except a never-polled future whose environment holds no linear value and no exclusive loan (it emits a `not_started` record). | LR 5.5, 12.3 |
| LANG-05-09 | Positional arguments first, then named in any order; each parameter bound once; parameter names are exported API. A pun `wanted` is `wanted: wanted`: after a named argument, and anywhere in a class constructor; before the first named argument a bare name is positional; an owned ownership-bearing local is written `name: move name`, never punned. | LR 5.8, X-345 |

Related, stated in LR 4.5: shadowing a visible binding is `E-NAM-003`.

## Diagnostics

| Code | Trigger | Correction | LR |
|---|---|---|---|
| E-NAM-001 | assignment to an undeclared name | declare it with `let mut`, or fix the name | LR 5.1 |
| E-NAM-002 | assignment to an immutable binding or a parameter | declare it `let mut`; a parameter is never reassignable, so copy it into a `let mut` local | LR 5.1 |
| E-NAM-003 | `let` shadows a visible binding | choose a new name | LR 4.5 |
| E-TYP-010 | non-`Bool` condition (`if n`, `if maybe`) | compare explicitly: `n != 0`, `maybe != null` | LR 5.2 |
| E-TYP-110 | a path reaches the end of a non-`Void` function, or a block arm or `if`-expression branch does not end in `give` | add `return`/`fail` on that path, or `give` in the branch | LR 5.4 |
| E-TYP-120 | `give` outside a match arm or `if` expression, `recover` outside `catch`, `break`/`continue` outside a loop | move the statement into the construct it ends | LR 5.4 |
| E-ERR-001 | `fail` outside a `try` function | declare the function `try`, or handle the condition without failing | LR 5.4 |
| E-TYP-140 | unused non-`Void` expression statement (a call of an `@ignorable` function excepted) | `discard e`, or bind and use the value; declare the function `@ignorable` when most callers drop its result | LR 5.5 |
| E-OBL-001 | `discard` of a linear value (a never-polled future holding nothing linear and no exclusive loan excepted) | consume it: `or fail`, `or recover v`, `catch`, `match`, `await`, launch | LR 5.5, 12.3 |
| E-SYN-004 | outcome operators, `??` and `&&`/`\|\|` mixed without parentheses | parenthesise the intended grouping | LR 5.6 |
| E-SYN-000 | not a sentence of the grammar (for example `f() or fail ?? 0`) | split the expression; `let v = f() or fail` on its own line | LR 5.6 |
| E-OWN-012 | a later argument moves, assigns or exclusively loans a place an earlier argument reserved | evaluate the conflicting argument into a binding first | LR 5.7 |
| E-TYP-130 | positional after named, unknown parameter name, parameter bound twice, too many arguments | fix the argument list | LR 5.8 |
| E-TYP-050 | a parameter without a default is not bound | pass it | LR 5.8 |

## Correction patterns

### E-NAM-002: assignment to an immutable binding (LR 5.1)

```fortis
// reject: E-NAM-002
pure func next(n: Int<0..9>) Int {
  let x = n
  x = n + 1                 // reject: E-NAM-002
  return x
}

test "next" {
  expect next(1) == 2
}
```

```fortis
// accept
pure func next(n: Int<0..9>) Int {
  let mut x: Int<0..10> = n
  x = n + 1
  return x
}

test "next" {
  expect next(1) == 2
}
```

### E-TYP-010: non-`Bool` condition (LR 5.2)

```fortis
// reject: E-TYP-010
pure func describe(n: Int) StringView from static {
  if n {                    // reject: E-TYP-010
    return "non-zero"
  }
  return "zero"
}

test "describe" {
  expect describe(0) == "zero"
}
```

```fortis
// accept
pure func describe(n: Int) StringView from static {
  if n != 0 {
    return "non-zero"
  }
  return "zero"
}

test "describe" {
  expect describe(0) == "zero"
  expect describe(3) == "non-zero"
}
```

### E-TYP-110: a path without `return` (LR 5.4)

The record is reported at the function head.

```fortis
// reject: E-TYP-110
pure func sign(n: Int) Int {        // reject: E-TYP-110
  if n < 0 {
    return -1
  }
}

test "sign" {
  expect sign(-4) == -1
}
```

```fortis
// accept
pure func sign(n: Int) Int {
  if n < 0 {
    return -1
  }
  if n == 0 {
    return 0
  }
  return 1
}

test "sign" {
  expect sign(-4) == -1
  expect sign(0) == 0
  expect sign(9) == 1
}
```

### E-TYP-120: `give` outside an `if` expression or arm (LR 5.4)

```fortis
// reject: E-TYP-120
pure func pick(flag: Bool) Int {
  if flag {
    give 1                  // reject: E-TYP-120
  }
  return 0
}

test "pick" {
  expect pick(false) == 0
}
```

```fortis
// accept
pure func pick(flag: Bool) Int {
  return if flag { give 1 } else { give 0 }
}

test "pick" {
  expect pick(true) == 1
  expect pick(false) == 0
}
```

### E-TYP-140: unused value (LR 5.5)

```fortis
// reject: E-TYP-140
pure func double(n: Int<0..1000>) Int => n * 2

test "double" {
  double(4)                 // reject: E-TYP-140
  expect double(2) == 4
}
```

```fortis
// accept
pure func double(n: Int<0..1000>) Int => n * 2

test "double" {
  discard double(4)
  expect double(2) == 4
}
```

### E-SYN-004: mixed operator families (LR 5.6)

```fortis
// reject: E-SYN-004
pure func choose(a: Bool, b: Bool?, c: Bool) Bool {
  return a || b ?? c        // reject: E-SYN-004
}

test "choose" {
  expect choose(false, null, true)
}
```

```fortis
// accept
pure func choose(a: Bool, b: Bool?, c: Bool) Bool {
  return a || (b ?? c)
}

test "choose" {
  expect choose(false, null, true)
  expect !choose(false, false, true)
}
```

### E-OWN-012: a reservation broken by a later argument (LR 5.7)

```fortis
// reject: E-OWN-012
class Buffer {
  export bytes: Int
}

func update(target: editable Buffer, size: Int) {
  target.bytes = size
}

func consume(b: owned Buffer) Int => b.bytes

test "update" {
  let mut buffer = Buffer(bytes: 0)
  update(editable buffer, consume(move buffer))   // reject: E-OWN-012
  expect buffer.bytes == 0
}
```

```fortis
// accept
class Buffer {
  export bytes: Int
}

func update(target: editable Buffer, size: Int) {
  target.bytes = size
}

func size(b: Buffer) Int => 7

test "update" {
  let mut buffer = Buffer(bytes: 0)
  let n = size(buffer)
  update(editable buffer, n)
  expect buffer.bytes == 7
}
```

### E-TYP-130 and E-TYP-050: argument binding (LR 5.8)

```fortis
// reject: E-TYP-130
pure func area(width: Int<0..100>, height: Int<0..100>) Int => width * height

test "area" {
  expect area(width: 2, depth: 3) == 6    // reject: E-TYP-130
}
```

```fortis
// reject: E-TYP-050
pure func area(width: Int<0..100>, height: Int<0..100>) Int => width * height

test "area" {
  expect area(width: 2) == 6              // reject: E-TYP-050
}
```

```fortis
// accept
pure func area(width: Int<0..100>, height: Int<0..100>) Int => width * height

test "area" {
  expect area(2, height: 3) == 6
  expect area(height: 3, width: 2) == 6
}
```

### `@ignorable` instead of `discard` (LR 5.5)

A function whose result most callers do not need is declared `@ignorable` once, and its call statements drop the
result without `discard` (LR 5.5, X-345). A linear result can never be ignorable (`E-TYP-150`).

```fortis
// accept
@ignorable
func remember(seen: editable Set[Int], n: Int) Bool {
  return seen.add(n)
}

test "remember" {
  let mut seen: Set[Int] = Set.default()
  remember(editable seen, 4)
  expect seen.count() == 1
}
```

## Facts used when writing code

- Literal booleans, `if` expressions and `match` give values; `if` without `else` is a statement only (LR 5.2).
- Ranges `a..b` (inclusive) and `a..<b` (exclusive) exist only in `for` headers and refinement types (LR 5.6).
- `for x in p` takes a read loan of `p` for the loop and binds read loans of the elements; `for x in move p`
  consumes `p` and binds owned elements (LR 5.3).
- Labels: `outer: for …`, then `break outer` / `continue outer`; `break` carries no value (LR 5.3).
- `return`/`fail` inside a lambda refer to the lambda; `give`/`recover` never cross a function or lambda
  boundary (LR 5.4).
- `await f() or fail` is `(await f()) or fail`; `copy await f()` is a parse error: markers take places (LR 5.6).
- Defaults are pure, non-allocating constant expressions re-evaluated at each call (LR 5.8). No user variadics:
  take `ListView[T]` and pass `List.of(…)` (LR 5.8).
- Temporaries drop at the end of the full statement in reverse creation order (LR 5.7).

## Linear consuming loops in v0.1

`for item in move items` owns each item. If its type is linear, consume it on every path before body end or
`continue`. Early exits cannot drop the hidden unvisited remainder, and unwind or cancellation points cannot
leave it live (LR 5.3). See [Outcomes and failures](10-outcomes.md#consuming-every-loop-item) for the
`E-OBL-001` and `E-OBL-005` correction pairs. Moving a `ListView` still only lends elements.

---
source: docs/agent/06-types.md
---

# Types (LR 6)

<!-- covers: LR 6 -->
*Agent mode. Human mode: [Types](../guide/06-types.md). Source of truth: LR 6. Proof rules for integer
operators and indexing (LR 6.3, 6.4, 6.7) are in [Proofs](06-proofs.md), the complete reference for Language 1.0's
interval domain; SP-18's further rules are a later edition (X-146).*

> Preview: normalisation, Unicode case mapping and the collections `OrderedMap`, `FixedList`, `FixedMap` and `VariantMap` beyond their syntax (LR 6.6, LR 6.7) arrive in v0.4. Refinements (LR 6.3), newtypes (LR 6.9), generics (LR 6.10) and conversions (LR 6.13) are in v0.1; `derive Default` (LR 6.10) is in v0.0.2.

## Rules

| Rule | Statement | LR |
|---|---|---|
| LANG-06-01 | Nominal identity survives calls, storage, serialisation and FFI: distinct declarations never interchange, whatever their representation. | LR 6.1, 6.9 |
| LANG-06-02 | A refinement is a structural subtype of its base and of every refinement containing it; the reverse is never implicit; the interval domain is exactly LR 6.3's, with no further inference. | LR 6.3 |
| LANG-06-03 | Untrusted values pass the checked `as` conversion (also spelled `validate` in v0.1) before holding a refined or nominal type. | LR 6.3, 6.9, 6.13 |
| LANG-06-04 | Integer, `Decimal` and the listed float operations agree bit-exactly across VM and native. | LR 6.4, 6.5 |
| LANG-06-05 | Float operators are total, strict IEEE 754; float refinements are rejected. | LR 6.3, 6.5 |
| LANG-06-06 | `Map`/`Set` keys implement Hashable and Equatable; iteration is deterministic per build (first-insertion order). | LR 6.7 |
| LANG-06-07 | The trivial and copyable sets are exactly those of LR 6.11. | LR 6.11 |
| LANG-06-08 | Optional, `Bool` and `Outcome` never convert into one another. | LR 6.8 |
| LANG-06-09 | Linear values are consumed exactly once on every path. | LR 6.12 |
| LANG-06-10 | Coherence: an implementation of an interface for a type lives in the package defining one of them; overlaps are rejected. | LR 6.10, 9.5 |
| LANG-06-11 | A call whose type arguments are fixed neither by its arguments nor by its expected type is rejected. | LR 6.10 |
| LANG-06-12 | No associated call on a type parameter (`T.default()`, `T.create()`): `E-TYP-170`; a call of a method of `T`'s interface bound runs on every backend (X-180). | LR 6.10 |
| LANG-06-13 | An `implement` block's target is a non-generic class or enum the program declares (`E-TYP-171`); an accepted block behaves as its target listing the interface (X-180). | LR 9.5 |
| LANG-06-14 | `x as T` resolves at compile time to exactly one conversion for the pair, a table row or a declared one (`E-TYP-180`); an identity is `E-TYP-181`; a built-in conversion is total or fails exactly as the table lists, alike on every backend; a newtype unwrap keeps its representation refinement and is `E-NAM-004` outside its declaring module (X-475, X-552). | LR 6.13 |
| LANG-06-15 | A class or enum declares or explicitly derives its conversions, one per pair, keyed by the whole type: a pair declared twice is `E-TYP-182`, a member for a pair the table decides is `E-TYP-183`, a generic class or enum and a newtype have no `convert` member (`E-TYP-184`); a consuming member takes `move x as T` (X-475, X-551). | LR 6.13 |
| LANG-06-16 | The functional methods take the callback types their signatures state: `pure fn` where the method only computes (`E-TYP-040` for a lambda that does not qualify), `fn mut` for `each`, an outcome-returning function for the `try` methods; a method returning elements requires `Copyable`; a `pure` function never calls `each` or `tryEach` (`E-EFF-001`); every backend runs them with the same results and visit order. | LR 6.7 |

## Diagnostics

| Code | Trigger | Correction | LR |
|---|---|---|---|
| E-TYP-040 | an `Outcome[T]` passed where `T` is expected | consume the outcome first (`let v = f() or fail`) | LR 10.1 |
| E-TYP-040 | `?.method()` calls an editable, consuming or `try` method | test for null, then call with the required mode and handle any outcome | LR 6.8 |
| E-TYP-090 | enum text derivation has payloads, type parameters, ASCII-case-clashing names or a source other than `String` | use a non-generic payload-free enum with distinct names, or write the conversion | LR 6.13 |
| E-TYP-040 | an interpolated string bound to a `StringView` binding | annotate the binding `String`, or drop the annotation | LR 3.5 |
| E-TYP-040 | a container or view whose type argument differs only in its refinement, in any direction (`List[Int<0..5>]` as a `List[Int]`, or the reverse as `E-REF-001`) | keep one refinement per container type; convert element by element with `map`, or validate each element (X-514) | LR 6.3 |
| E-REF-001 | a literal outside its target refinement, a value the interval rules do not prove, or a `List[Int]` where a `List[Int<0..5>]` is expected (its elements are never proved) | widen the declared type, or convert with `x as T` and handle the outcome | LR 3.5, 6.3 |
| E-TYP-020 | a refinement that is not of its base: a float base (`Float<0..1>`), a base the forms do not name, a measure the base lacks, a bound that does not fold at compile time, an empty or inverted range (`Int<5..1>`), or one outside the base's own range (`UInt8<0..300>`) | refine an integer representation (for example a count of thousandths), fix the range, or use a `const` bound of the base type (X-512) | LR 6.3 |
| E-REF-003 | a length-refined collection loaned `editable` or mutated | mutate an unrefined collection, then convert with `move c as T` | LR 6.3 |
| E-TYP-030 | a tuple, record or variant map in an exported signature (aspect parameters and the `fortis` package's own signatures excepted), or a non-exported type in one | declare and export a named class | LR 6.9, 4.4 |
| E-TYP-090 | `derive I` where a field does not implement `I`; a derivation rule not met; the codec pair on a non-`Encodable`/`Decodable` type; a `Set`/`Map` whose key lacks `Hashable` and `Equatable` (X-615) | implement or derive the interface for the field or key type, change the type, or write the implementation by hand | LR 6.10, 6.7 |
| E-TYP-160 | type arguments not fixed (`let names = List.default()`; `null` fixes nothing) | annotate the receiving binding: `let names: List[String] = List.default()` | LR 6.10 |
| E-TYP-170 | an associated call on a type parameter (`T.default()`, `T.fromText(text)`, `T.create()`) | take a value of `T`, or a function that makes one (`make: fn() T`), as a parameter (X-180) | LR 6.10 |
| E-TYP-180 | `x as T` with no conversion for the pair: no row of the built-in table and no declared member; conversions never chain by search | convert through the named function the record cites (`Decimal.fromFloat(x, scale, mode)`), or in steps the table has (`s as Int as Decimal`); declare a `convert` member for a class or enum pair | LR 6.13 |
| E-TYP-181 | `x as T` where `x` already has type `T`: two names of one range, a refinement to its base or a wider refinement | drop the `as`: the value is already a `T` | LR 6.13 |
| E-TYP-182 | two conversions declared for one pair (a `convert to` and a `convert from` naming each other, or two members) | delete one: a pair converts by one declaration, in the body of its source or its target | LR 6.13 |
| E-TYP-183 | a `convert` member for a pair the built-in table already decides, the identity included | delete the member: the pair converts without a declaration | LR 6.13 |
| E-TYP-184 | a `convert` member on a generic class or enum or a newtype, or one whose other type is a refinement | wrap the value in a non-generic class the program declares; a refinement target stays the table's `validate` row | LR 6.13 |
| E-NAM-004 | a newtype unwrap (`p as Int`) outside its declaring module, or an editing or consuming method of a collection newtype called outside it (X-552, X-581) | unwrap inside the declaring module, or add a reading method there; edit a collection newtype inside its module | LR 6.9 |
| E-OWN-002 | `copy x` of a type parameter without `T implements Copyable`, or a loaned `T` a call returns made owned without that bound (X-513) | add the bound, or take and return the `T` by loan only | LR 6.10, 6.12 |
| E-OWN-030 | `trivial class` with a non-trivial field (reported at the class) | drop `trivial`, or make every field trivial | LR 6.11 |
| E-OWN-002 | `copy` of a non-copyable type (`Shared`, `Weak`, `Mutex`, loans, futures, closures…) | `retain()` for `Shared`/`Weak`; otherwise move or loan | LR 6.11, 7.5 |
| E-OBL-001 | a linear value dropped, overwritten or discarded (except `discard` of a never-polled future whose environment holds no linear value and no exclusive loan, LR 12.3) | consume it (`Must.discharge(move m)`; outcomes: `or fail`, `or recover`, `catch`, `match`) | LR 6.12, 12.3 |
| E-OBL-003 | a generic function holding its own `T` by value, or a user generic class or enum (X-611), instantiated with a linear type without declaring `T: linear` | declare `where T: linear` and consume the value, or take the `T` by loan only; a class or enum writes the bound in a `where` clause at the end of its head | LR 6.12, 10.7 |
| E-TYP-010 | an optional used as a condition | `x != null` | LR 6.8 |
| E-MIX-001 | deriving an interface the class also implements by hand | keep one of the two | LR 6.10 |

## Built-in types (LR 6.2)

`Void` `Never` `Bool`; `Int8` `Int16` `Int32` `Int64` `UInt8` `UInt16` `UInt32` `UInt64` (`Int` = `Int64`,
`UInt` = `UInt64`, `Byte` = `UInt8`); `Float32` `Float`; `Decimal` `BigInt`; `String` `StringView` `Bytes`
`BytesView`; `Duration` `Instant` `Timestamp`; `List[T]` `Array[T, N]` `ListView[T]` `Map[K, V]`
`OrderedMap[K, V]` `Set[T]` `FixedList[T, N]` `FixedMap[K, V, N]`; tuples, anonymous records,
`VariantMap[E, V]`; `T?`; `Outcome[T]` `Failure` `Report`; `Future[T]` `Task[T]` `TaskCompletion[T]` `Shared[T]`
`Weak[T]` `Mutex[T]` `AtomicInt` `AtomicBool`; `fn`/`fn mut`/`fn once` types. `N` is an integer literal; no
generics over `N`. `List.of(...items: T)` is the only variadic form (standard library only) (LR 6.2).

## Facts used when writing code

- Refinement forms: `Int<0..100>`, `Int<0..<100>`, `Int<1..>`, `Int<..0>`, `String<scalars: 1..120>`,
  `Bytes<length: 0..65536>`, `List[T]<length: 0..100>`; type position only (LR 6.3). Each bound is an integer
  literal or a `const` of the base type folded at compile time (`Int<0..top>`, X-512); an empty or inverted
  range, one outside the base's own range, a base or measure the forms do not name, or a bound that does not
  fold, is `E-TYP-020`. Type arguments of a container or view are invariant in their refinement (X-514). Optional values,
  tuple elements and record fields may widen as values; editable loans preserve their types invariantly
  through every member (LR 6.3, 6.9; X-685, X-686, X-712).
- `x as T` is the checked conversion (LR 6.13): into a refinement always fallible (`Outcome[T]`,
  `refinement.out_of_range`); into a newtype total when the representation is proved, fallible otherwise.
  `T.validate(x)` and `Int<0..100>.validate(x)` are the retired call spelling, still accepted, always an
  outcome; `fortis fmt` rewrites them (X-552, X-553).
- Integer arithmetic (LR 6.4): an operator the checker cannot prove safe is written as the left operand of an
  outcome operator, `a * b + c or fail`, and is the checked operation, failing `numeric.overflow`,
  `numeric.divide_by_zero`, `numeric.shift_range` (X-345). The named families, on `Int` only (the
  sized integer types have none yet; v0.4): checked `Int.add/sub/mul/div/rem/shiftLeft` → `Outcome` (the same
  operations; `fortis fmt` writes the operator where the two are equivalent); `wrapping…` and `saturating…` are total. Division truncates toward zero; `%` has the dividend's sign; `>>` arithmetic on signed, logical on unsigned.
- The success value of a checked intrinsic has the interval of the operation on its operands (LR 6.3, X-93), so
  `Int.div(-7, 2) or recover 0` is `E-REF-001` (0 is outside `[-3, -3]`); annotate the binding `Int`.
- Floats (LR 6.5): no `Equatable`/`Hashable`/`Comparable`; `==` is IEEE; keys via `Float.totalOrder(x)` or
  `Float.bitsEqual(a, b)`; display is shortest round-trip with a fractional part (`2000.0`), `NaN`, `Infinity`.
- `Decimal` (LR 6.5): no operators; `Decimal.add/sub/mul/div/rem` → `Outcome[Decimal]`; scale rules: add/sub larger
  scale, mul sum of scales, div largest that fits, half-even when over 28 digits; `Decimal.round(v, scale, mode)`
  with `RoundingMode.HalfEven|HalfAwayFromZero|TowardZero|AwayFromZero`; displays with exactly its scale.
- Text (LR 6.6): literal is `StringView from static`; implicit literal-to-`String` conversion allocates (refused
  in `noalloc`); `view as String` is the explicit copy (`String.from(view)` retired, accepted, fmt rewrites it);
  no integer indexing; `byteCount()` O(1), `scalarCount()` O(n),
  `slice(from, to)` → `Outcome[StringView from view]`, `scalarAt(i)` → `Outcome[Scalar]`; `text.Builder`
  `create/append/appendLine/appendScalar/finish`.
- Text essentials on `String` and `StringView` alike (X-595; none fails, none indexes by integer):
  `trim`/`trimStart`/`trimEnd` → `StringView from self` (no allocation; a loan of the text), `find(needle)` →
  `Int<0..>?` (a scalar offset; the empty needle is found at 0), `contains`, `startsWith`, `endsWith` → `Bool`,
  `split(sep)` → `List[String]` (every piece kept; an empty separator gives one piece), `lines()` →
  `List[String]` (a line ends at `\n`, a `\r\n` pair ends together; text after the last terminator is a line
  only when not empty), `replace(old, new)` → `String`, `asciiUpper`/`asciiLower` → `String` (ASCII only,
  X-596), `repeat(times: Int<0..>)` → `String`, `String.join(parts, sep)` → `String`; split, lines, replace,
  case, repeat and join allocate. Parsing is the conversion `text as Int or fail` (LR 6.13), never a text
  method.
- Collections (LR 6.7): `list[i]` needs a proof ([Proofs](06-proofs.md)); otherwise `get(i)` → `(alias T from
  self)?`, `at(i)` → `Outcome[T]`; `set(i, v)` → `Outcome[Void]`; `push(item)` → `Void`; `pop()` → `T?`;
  `clear()` empties the list and is rejected for linear elements (`E-OBL-001`, LR 10.7). `Map.set/get/count`,
  `Set.add` (→ `Bool`, true when new) `/contains/count`; iteration in first-insertion order, replacement keeps the
  position; neither has an `iterate()` or a cursor of its own in v0.1 (D-58, D-535); `for entry in map` binds a
  `(key, value)` tuple by read loan. `get` on a `Map[String, V]` takes a `StringView` key, so `counts.get(word)`
  takes a view or a `String` with no `copy`; `set` takes an owned key.
- Collections in a functional style (LR 6.7, X-479; `List`, `ListView`, beside the loops, which stay): `each`,
  `tryEach` (callback `editable fn mut`, effects allowed), `map`, `tryMap`, `filter`, `fold`, `tryFold`, `any`,
  `all`, `find`, `indexWhere`, `contains`, `sortedBy`, `enumerate`, `zip`, `take`, `skip`, `flatMap`,
  `chunked`, `groupBy`. Callbacks that only compute are `pure fn` (an I/O lambda is `E-TYP-040`); a `pure`
  function cannot call `each`/`tryEach` (`E-EFF-001`, LR 11.3); methods returning elements require
  `T implements Copyable` (`take`, `skip`, `enumerate`, `zip`, `chunked`, `sortedBy`, `groupBy`, `keys`, `values`, the
  set operations, `filter`); methods that only look do not. `try` callbacks return `Outcome[U]` (a plain value
  is `E-TYP-040`) and stop at the first failure; the call is handled on the line. `Map.each/keys/values`;
  `Set.each/union/intersection/difference`. `sortedBy` is stable; `groupBy` keys in first-appearance order;
  `chunked(size: Int<1..>)`. Reading traversals keep obligations in their owner; bind a fresh linear list
  before borrowing it. Non-failing map may produce linear results; tryMap results and fold accumulators
  must be non-linear (LR 10.7).
- `Deque[T]` and `SortedSet[T]` are written in Fortis in `fortis.collections` and imported from it (LR 6.7, X-576,
  X-577): built with `default()`/`fromList(items)` (variadic `of` is `List`'s alone); not `Copyable` (`copy` is
  `E-OWN-002`; `toList()` copies the items and `fromList` consumes an owned list); `Deque` pushes and pops at both ends amortised O(1) and holds
  resources; `SortedSet` needs `T implements Comparable`, keeps members ascending, each once, with `between(low, high)`,
  `union`, `intersection`, `difference`; a `for` over either, or over any class implementing `Iterable[T, I]`,
  walks its cursor (D-545). `Array.get(i)` → `(alias T from self)?` (null outside `[0, N)`), `asView()` →
  `ListView[T] from self` (X-578); `Array.filled` writes its size on the call, `Array[Int, 3].filled(7)`
  (D-399).
- Keys (LR 6.7, X-615): every written or inferred `Set[T]`, `Map[K, V]` requires `Hashable` and `Equatable` on the key
  or element, `E-TYP-090` even when empty, inside nested types and after instantiation; generic code needs
  `where K implements Hashable` (which grants `Equatable`); a class has no interface `where` bound in v0.1, so
  a field `Map[K, V]` over the class's own unbounded parameter is rejected; tuples and anonymous records are
  never keys; an enum is a key only by derivation or implementation. Make a key with `derive Equatable,
  Hashable`; a hand-written `hash` writes nothing (`Hasher` has no members in Language 1.0), so membership is
  decided by `equals` alone (X-516).
- Optionals (LR 6.8): `T` → `T?` implicit; `??` lazy; `a?.f`; `match` with `present(x)` / `null`; narrowing after
  `x != null`, after `if x == null { return … }`, and in `x != null && e`; `maybe.map(fn(x) => …)` → `U?` is
  the one method called with `.` on a `T?` without narrowing (`null` stays `null`; X-479).
- Optional method calls (LR 6.8, X-632): `a?.m(args)` evaluates `a` once; null skips arguments and returns null.
  Present calls `m`; `U` becomes `U?`, `U?` stays `U?`. Chains, mixin and interface methods resolve as after a
  null test. Only read receivers and non-`try` methods in v0.1 (`E-TYP-040` otherwise). Effects still count;
  returned loans and views retain the receiver's owner through optional injection and chaining (LR 7.6,
  LR 7.7). The formatter keeps `?.m()` and `map(fn(x) => x.m())` as written.
- Tuples `t.0`; records `{ name: a }`; `VariantMap[E, V]` literal `{ Found: 200, NotFound: 404 }` with one entry
  per variant; `(fn(Int) Bool)?` is an optional function (LR 6.9).
- Newtypes (LR 6.9): `type Name = Repr` is always nominal with a private representation. Build with `raw as
  Name` (fallible unless proved, LR 6.13) or `Name(x)`, judged as a call: a literal proved in range, a value of
  the representation type, or a value whose interval is proved; unproved is `E-REF-001`, another type
  `E-TYP-040` (X-511); the retired `Name.validate(raw)` stays accepted. Implements Equatable, Hashable,
  Comparable and Displayable exactly when the representation does, whatever it is (X-511); trivial over a
  trivial representation. Unwrap with `name as Rep` in the declaring module only (total, keeps the
  representation's refinement; `E-NAM-004` outside; X-552); a linear representation wraps only when proved
  (`E-OBL-001` otherwise). Collection newtypes (X-581): reading methods (`self`) visible everywhere, editing
  and consuming ones (`editable self`, `owned self`) only inside the declaring module (`E-NAM-004` outside);
  reading iteration follows the representation; a method returning `List[T]` returns `List[T]`; no associated
  functions, indexing, conversion or interchange. A newtype declares no `convert` member.
- Generics (LR 6.10): `[T]`, `where T implements I` after the return type; type arguments are always inferred,
  never written at a call. A written expected type fixes the parameters it names first; arguments fix the
  rest (disagreeing arguments join to their common type, two refinements of one base to the hull, else
  `E-TYP-040`; `null` fixes nothing). A parameter the result names inside a type argument takes an integer argument's
  base type: `List.of(small)` with `small: Int<0..3>` is a `List[Int]`; write `let xs: List[Int<0..9>] =
  List.of(small, big)` to keep a refinement (X-513). In a body `x: T` is a loan: returning, storing or passing
  it `owned` needs a marker (`E-OWN-001`); `copy x` needs `T implements Copyable` (`E-OWN-002` without); a
  loaned `T` a call returns never becomes owned without that bound. No associated call on `T` (`E-TYP-170`,
  X-180). Native lowering gives `T` exactly the Rust bounds its `where` names (X-515). Instantiation depth
  budget 32 (`E-LIM-001`). A generic class's constructor takes its arguments from the written type, else the
  expected type.
- Derivable (LR 6.10): `Equatable`, `Hashable`, `Comparable`, `Displayable`, `Encodable`,
  `Decodable`, `Codec`; derived `Comparable` orders a class by its fields in declaration order and an enum by
  variant order, then payload fields (X-516); `Default` (field initialisers first; a class gets `Name.default()`,
  no arguments; written without its call, `Name.default` is that function's value, X-516); `derive convert
  from S` (total borrowed field-wise; a missing, private or non-`Copyable` field or a fallible or consuming
  field conversion is `E-TYP-090`). `==`/`!=` call `equals`, `< <= > >=` call `compare`, and containers find a
  key by the same `equals`/`hash`, on every backend; a core type's `equals`/`compare` are ordinary callable
  methods; core `hash` is not callable (X-516). The retired `From[S]`/`to()`/`derive From[S]` stay accepted; `fortis fmt` rewrites them
  (LR 6.13).
- Canonical codec (LR 6.10): `toText()`/`fromText(input)` (JSON, declaration order), `toBytes()`/
  `fromBytes(input)`; failures `codec.invalid`, `codec.unknown_field`, or the refinement's own failure. Encodable
  derivation needs exported, encodable fields; secrets, authorities, loans, closures, futures and tasks are never
  encodable.
- Trivial (LR 6.11): primitives, `Decimal`, `Scalar`, time types, newtypes over trivial, enums/optionals/tuples/
  records of trivial, `trivial class`. Copyable: trivial, `String`, `Bytes`, `BigInt`, collections and
  aggregates of copyable. Not copyable: `Shared`, `Weak`, `Mutex`, atomics, loans, views, resources, `Future`,
  `Task`, `Outcome`, `Failure`, closures.
- Linear (LR 6.12): `Outcome[T]`, `Failure`, `Future[T]`, `Task[T]`, `Must`, `fn once` capturing one, and any
  type that can contain one. Type parameters are non-linear unless `T: linear`; a generic function holding a
  `T` by value declares it and consumes the value, and a user generic class or enum is instantiated at a linear
  argument only with `T: linear` on the corresponding parameter (`E-OBL-003`), written in a `where` clause at
  the end of its head, which accepts linear bounds only (X-611).

## Conversions (LR 6.13)

- One operator: `expression as Type`; binds tighter than arithmetic and comparison (`a as Decimal * b` is
  `(a as Decimal) * b`), chains left to right. A `<` directly after the target opens a refinement, so a
  comparison writes parentheses: `(n as Int) < 5` (X-550).
- Resolution is static, to exactly one conversion for the pair: a table row, the base-into-refinement row, or a
  member or explicit derivation a class or enum declares. No conversion is `E-TYP-180` (conversions never chain
  by search); an identity, two names of one range and a refinement to its base or a wider one are `E-TYP-181`.
- Total conversions have type `T`; fallible ones `Outcome[T]`, handled on the line (`or fail`, `or recover`,
  `catch`, `match`). Nothing rounds: `Float` into an integer or `Decimal` has no conversion; write
  `Decimal.fromFloat(x, scale, mode)`.
- Built-in rows: integer widening total, narrowing `conversion.out_of_range`; integer → `Decimal` total;
  `Decimal` → integer `conversion.not_integral`/`conversion.out_of_range`; `Int32` and smaller → `Float` total,
  `Int`/`Int64`/`UInt`/`UInt64` → `Float` `conversion.not_exact`; `Float`/`Float32` → `String` total, and there
  is no `String` → `Float` row; the integers, `Decimal`, `Bool`, `Scalar`, `Float`, `Float32` → `String` total
  (canonical text, allocates); `String`/`StringView` → an integer type, `Decimal`, `Bool` fallible
  (`conversion.parse`, `conversion.out_of_range`); `StringView` → `String` total (allocates);
  `Bytes`/`BytesView` → `String` `conversion.not_utf8`; `String`/`StringView` → `Bytes` total; `Scalar` → `Int`
  total; `Int` → `Scalar` `conversion.out_of_range`; base → refinement `refinement.out_of_range` (fallible even
  for a proved value); base → newtype total when proved, else `refinement.out_of_range`; newtype → its
  representation total, declaring module only (`E-NAM-004` outside).
- Failure payloads: `conversion.out_of_range` (`value`, `low`, `high`), `conversion.not_integral` (`value`),
  `conversion.not_exact` (`value`), `conversion.parse` (`text`), `conversion.not_utf8` (`position`).
- The operand is passed as to a read-loan parameter: a bare place is loaned, `move x as T` moves in, `copy x as
  T` converts a copy; into a new `String`/`Bytes` allocates (refused in `noalloc`).
- Members on a class or enum: `convert to T`, `try convert to T`, `convert from S(s)`, `try convert from S(s)`;
  `try` makes `x as T` an `Outcome[T]`; the body is a method body whose returns give the target (the declaring
  type for `convert from`); `self`/`s` is a read loan unless the head writes `owned`, and a consuming member is
  used as `move x as T`; visibility as a method's (no `export`: module only). One conversion per pair keyed by
  the whole type (`E-TYP-182`); a member for a pair the table decides is `E-TYP-183`; a generic class or enum
  and a newtype declare none (`E-TYP-184`); a pair of two foreign types has no body to hold a member.
- Retired, accepted in v0.1, rewritten by `fortis fmt` resolving by identity (X-552, X-553): `From[S]` (a
  legacy implementation supplies the pair of a total borrowed `convert from S`), `T.from(x)`, `x.to()` (kept
  with a note where no expected target is written), `derive From[S]` → `derive convert from S`,
  `String.from(view)` → `view as String`, `T.validate(x)` → `x as T`. A directly enclosing failure handler
  is dropped when the formatter proves the conversion always succeeds, leaving `x as T` or the plain value
  for a proved structural refinement. An unproved conversion keeps its handler. Only an outcome-valued position
  keeps the wrapper: `Outcome.success(x as T)` when total, `Outcome.success(x)` for a refinement already proved.

## Enum text derivation (LR 6.13)

X-631: `derive convert from String` on a non-generic payload-free enum
generates exact fallible borrowed pairs for both `String` and `StringView`; literals use the latter. Match
the whole name, ASCII case-insensitive, without trimming; call `trim()` explicitly. Failure is
`conversion.parse` with owned `text` and `variants` (names in declaration order, separated by `, `).
Non-ASCII scalars compare exactly. Either generated pair conflicts with a member for that pair
(`E-TYP-182`); both have the enum's visibility. No reverse conversion is generated; use Displayable for
interpolation. Payloads, generic enums, clashing names and other source types are `E-TYP-090`.
## Correction patterns

### E-TYP-040: a raw value where a newtype is expected (LR 6.9, LR 10.1)

```fortis
// reject: E-TYP-040
type CustomerId = Int<1..>

pure func lookup(id: CustomerId) Int => 1

pure func fromInput(raw: Int) Int {
  return lookup(raw)                  // reject: E-TYP-040
}

test "lookup" {
  expect fromInput(5) == 1
}
```

```fortis
// accept
type CustomerId = Int<1..>

pure func lookup(id: CustomerId) Int => 1

pure try func fromInput(raw: Int) Int {
  let id = raw as CustomerId or fail
  return lookup(id)
}

test "lookup" {
  let found = fromInput(5)
  expect found == 1
}
```

### E-REF-001: a literal outside its refinement (LR 3.5, LR 6.3)

```fortis
// reject: E-REF-001
pure func limit() Int<0..100> {
  let score: Int<0..100> = 140        // reject: E-REF-001
  return 100
}

test "limit" {
  expect limit() == 100
}
```

```fortis
// accept
pure func limit() Int<0..100> {
  let score: Int<0..100> = 100
  return score
}

test "limit" {
  expect limit() == 100
}
```

### E-REF-003: mutating a length-refined collection (LR 6.3)

```fortis
// reject: E-REF-003
pure func grow(start: List[Int]<length: 0..3>) Int {
  let mut items = copy start
  items.push(1)                       // reject: E-REF-003
  return items.count()
}

test "grow" {
  expect true
}
```

```fortis
// accept
pure try func three() List[Int]<length: 0..3> {
  let mut items: List[Int] = List.default()
  items.push(1)
  return move items as List[Int]<length: 0..3> or fail
}

test "three" {
  let items = three()
  expect items.count() == 1
}
```

### E-TYP-160: type arguments not fixed (LR 6.10)

```fortis
// reject: E-TYP-160
pure func names() Int {
  let found = List.default()          // reject: E-TYP-160
  return found.count()
}

test "names" {
  expect names() == 0
}
```

```fortis
// accept
pure func names() Int {
  let found: List[String] = List.default()
  return found.count()
}

test "names" {
  expect names() == 0
}
```

### E-TYP-030: a structural type in an exported signature (LR 6.9)

```fortis
// reject: E-TYP-030
export pure func bounds() (Int, Int) => (1, 2)     // reject: E-TYP-030

test "bounds" {
  expect bounds().0 == 1
}
```

```fortis
// accept
export class Bounds {
  export low: Int
  export high: Int
}

export pure func bounds() Bounds => Bounds(low: 1, high: 2)

test "bounds" {
  expect bounds().low == 1
}
```

### E-TYP-090: deriving an interface a field lacks (LR 6.10)

```fortis
// reject: E-TYP-090
class Reading derive Equatable {    // reject: E-TYP-090
  export celsius: Float
}

test "reading" {
  expect Reading(celsius: 1.5).celsius > 1.0
}
```

```fortis
// accept
class Reading derive Equatable {
  export celsius: Decimal
}

test "reading" {
  expect Reading(celsius: 1.5d) == Reading(celsius: 1.5d)
}
```

A `Set` element or `Map` key needs `Hashable` and `Equatable` even when the container is empty (LR 6.7).
Derive both on a class or enum whose fields support them. In generic functions, add `where K implements Hashable`;
that bound also grants its required `Equatable` interface.

```fortis
// reject: E-TYP-090
class Key { export n: Int }
func empty() Map[Key, Int] => Map.default()    // reject: E-TYP-090
```

```fortis
// accept
class Key derive Equatable, Hashable { export n: Int }
func empty() Map[Key, Int] => Map.default()
test "empty map" { expect empty().count() == 0 }
```

### E-TYP-020: a float refinement (LR 6.3)

```fortis
// reject: E-TYP-020
type Ratio = Float<0..1>              // reject: E-TYP-020

test "ratio" {
  expect true
}
```

```fortis
// accept
type BasisPoints = Int<0..10000>

test "ratio" {
  let half = 5000 as BasisPoints
  expect half == BasisPoints(5000)
}
```

### E-OWN-030: a trivial class with a non-trivial field (LR 6.11)

```fortis
// reject: E-OWN-030
trivial class Tag {                   // reject: E-OWN-030
  export name: String
}

test "tag" {
  expect Tag(name: "a").name == "a"
}
```

```fortis
// accept
class Tag {
  export name: String
}

test "tag" {
  expect Tag(name: "a").name == "a"
}
```

### E-OBL-001: a linear value dropped (LR 6.12)

```fortis
// reject: E-OBL-001
pure func witness() Int {
  let token = Must.create()           // reject: E-OBL-001
  return 1
}

test "witness" {
  expect witness() == 1
}
```

```fortis
// accept
pure func witness() Int {
  let token = Must.create()
  Must.discharge(move token)
  return 1
}

test "witness" {
  expect witness() == 1
}
```

### E-TYP-040: an interpolated string held as a view (LR 3.5, LR 6.6)

```fortis
// reject: E-TYP-040
pure func label(n: Int) Int {
  let text: StringView = "count ${n}"      // reject: E-TYP-040
  return text.scalarCount()
}

test "label" {
  expect label(3) == 7
}
```

```fortis
// accept
pure func label(n: Int) Int {
  let text: String = "count ${n}"
  return text.scalarCount()
}

test "label" {
  expect label(3) == 7
}
```

### E-TYP-090: enum names must be distinct under ASCII case comparison (LR 6.13)

```fortis
// reject: E-TYP-090
enum Size derive convert from String { // reject: E-TYP-090
  Large
  LARGE
}
```

```fortis
// accept
enum Size derive Equatable, convert from String {
  Small
  Large
}

test "trim and parse a size" {
  let size = "  LARGE  ".trim() as Size or recover Small
  expect size == Large
}
```

### E-TYP-040: test for null before editing the present value (LR 6.8)

```fortis
// reject: E-TYP-040
class Cell {
  func change(editable self) {}
}

func main() {
  let mut cell: Cell? = Cell()
  discard cell?.change() // reject: E-TYP-040
}
```

```fortis
// accept
class Cell {
  func change(editable self) {}
}

func main() {
  let mut cell: Cell? = Cell()
  if cell != null {
    cell.change()
  }
}
```

### E-OBL-001: consume the obligation on each optional path (LR 6.8)

Optional method arguments run only when the receiver is present. An argument cannot move an existing linear
value, including through a nested call or into a closure capture. Test for null and consume it on both branches.

```fortis
// reject: E-OBL-001
class Cell {
  func take(self, m: owned Must) Int { Must.discharge(move m)
    return 1 }
}
func main() {
  let cell: Cell? = null
  let m = Must.create()
  let n = cell?.take(move m) // reject: E-OBL-001
}
```

```fortis
// accept
class Cell {
  func take(self, m: owned Must) Int { Must.discharge(move m)
    return 1 }
}
func main() {
  let cell: Cell? = null
  let m = Must.create()
  match cell {
    present(c) => { let n = c.take(move m) }
    null => Must.discharge(move m)
  }
}
```

---
source: docs/agent/06-proofs.md

# Proofs for arithmetic and indexing (LR 6.3, 6.4, 6.7)

<!-- covers: LR 6.3, LR 6.4, LR 6.7 -->
*Agent mode. Human mode: [Proving arithmetic and indexing](../guide/06-proofs.md). Source of truth: LR 6.3,
LR 6.4 and LR 6.7.*

Language 1.0's interval domain is exactly the rules below; nothing else is inferred (LANG-06-02, LR 6.3). SP-18's
wider rules are a later edition (X-146).

## Rules

| Rule | Statement | LR |
|---|---|---|
| LANG-06-02 | Refinement subtyping is structural; the interval domain is exactly the rules of LR 6.3, with no further inference. | LR 6.3 |
| LANG-06-03 | An untrusted value reaches a refined or nominal type only through the checked `as` conversion (also spelled `validate` in v0.1); a proved value already meets its refinement, and `Name(value)` constructs a newtype over it. | LR 6.3, 6.9, 6.13 |
| LANG-05-04 | `for i in a..<b` / `a..b` gives the index the range's interval; the index is immutable. | LR 5.3, 6.3 |

## The domain (LR 6.3)

- Tracked: every integer-typed place of a function, as an interval within its base type.
- Sources: literal = exact; parameter or field = declared type; call result = declared return type, except the
  success value of a checked operation (a checked operator, or its named function `Int.add`, `Int.sub`, `Int.mul`,
  `Int.div`, `Int.rem`, `Int.shiftLeft`), which is the operation on its operands clipped to the type (X-93).
- `+ - *`: interval arithmetic. `/` and `%`: divisor interval must exclude 0; result is the quotient or remainder
  interval. `<<`: amount within [0, width-1].
- `%` with `m` = largest `|d|`: `a` ≥ 0 gives [0, m-1]; `a` ≤ 0 gives [-(m-1), 0]; otherwise [-(m-1), m-1].
- Narrowing: conditions `p < c`, `p <= c`, `p > c`, `p >= c`, `p == c`, `p != c` (`c` a literal, a `const` or a
  tracked place, narrowed too) in `if`, `while`, `match`; `&&` narrows by both; `else` gets the negation of a
  single comparison; a true branch ending in `return`, `fail`, `break`, `continue` or a `Never` call gives the
  negation to the rest of the block. `||` and calls never narrow.
- Join: hull of the incoming intervals.
- Loop header: every place assigned or invalidated in the body is widened to its declared type; a ranged `for`
  index keeps the range's interval. Refine loop counters (`let mut i: Int<0..1000> = 0`).
- Invalidation: an exclusive loan of the place, a prefix or a field (an `editable` argument, an `editable self`
  call on it, marked or not, an `editable` binding), or an `editable` capture of a closure that is called; the
  place returns to its declared type. Assignment replaces the facts with the assigned interval.
- Length facts: `i < p.count()` true branch gives `i` below `p`'s length; in `for i in a..<p.count()` the index is
  below the length throughout a body that neither assigns nor exclusively loans `p` (X-93); `i <= p.count()` does
  not permit indexing; `i >= p.count()` / `i > p.count()` give the bound in their `else`. Upper bound only: the
  lower bound comes from `i`'s type or `i >= 0`.
- Length-refined collections (`List[T]<length: …>`) are immutable: no `editable` loan, no mutation.

## Operators and indexing (LR 6.4, 6.7)

- Proof-required: integer `+ - * / % << >>` and unary `-`; the result type is the base refined to the result
  interval. No dependence on the build mode.
- Checked operators, the alternative needing no proof (X-345): `Int` arithmetic as the left operand of
  `or fail`/`or recover`/`catch` is a checked region; each unproved `+ - * / % <<` or unary `-` in it is the checked
  operation, failing `numeric.overflow`, `numeric.divide_by_zero` or `numeric.shift_range`, the first failure
  ending the region: `value = value * 10 + d or fail`. The region stops at calls, indexes,
  fields, comparisons and other operators: `f(a + b) or fail`, `a + b == c or fail` and `let s = a + b` stay
  `E-REF-002`; write `f(a + b or fail)`, `(a + b or fail) == c`, `let s = a + b or fail`. A fully proved region
  cannot fail: `or fail` on it is `E-TYP-040`. Only `Int` has a checked family; `>>` has none.
- Named alternatives: checked `Int.add`… (`Outcome[Int]`, the same failures; older code writes
  `Int.add(a, b) or fail`, and `fortis fmt` writes the operator where the two are equivalent); wrapping
  `Int.wrappingAdd`…; saturating `Int.saturatingAdd`….
- `list[i]` needs `i` ≥ 0 and below the length (known for `Array[T, N]`, length-refined lists, and the length
  facts above). Alternatives: `get(i)` → `T?`, `at(i)` → `Outcome[T]` failing `collection.index`.

## Diagnostics

| Code | Trigger | Correction | LR |
|---|---|---|---|
| E-REF-002 | an integer operator not proved safe (overflow, zero divisor, shift amount, `MIN / -1`) outside a checked region; an index not proved in bounds | refine the operands' types or test them first; else the checked operator, `a + b or fail`; for an index, `if i >= 0 && i < xs.count()`, or `get`/`at` | LR 6.4, 6.7 |
| E-REF-001 | a value whose interval is not within the target's refinement (assignment, return, argument, literal) | widen the target type, narrow first (a guard), or `x as T or fail` (the retired spelling `T.validate(x) or fail` still accepted) | LR 6.3, 3.5, 6.13 |
| E-REF-003 | a length-refined collection loaned `editable` or mutated | mutate an unrefined collection, then convert with `move c as T` | LR 6.3, 6.13 |

The records carry `required_range`, `proved_interval` and `widening_point`. Read the `status`
field before correcting ([records](records.md)): `violated` means the checker proved the rule
broken (a literal outside the target's range, such as `20` returned as an `Int<0..10>`, or a mutation of a
length-refined collection), so the program is wrong and the value or the type must change; `unproved` means it
could not prove the bound, which is not a claim that the program is wrong, and the correction is a proof (a
refinement or a guard) or the checked alternative.

## Correction patterns

### E-REF-002: an unproved operator (LR 6.4)

```fortis
// reject: E-REF-002
```
