# Rule index (LR D)

<!-- covers: LR D -->
*Agent mode. Human mode: [Rule index](../guide/appendix-d-rules.md). Source of truth: each LR section's rule
table; LR D for old IDs.*

Every `LANG-` rule, its section, a condensed statement and the agent page that carries its codes and correction
patterns. A diagnostic record's `rule` field names one of these IDs, or a `PROG-` or `PLAT-` ID.
The LR rule text is authoritative; the statements here are condensed (LR 0).

## LR 3-6

| Rule | LR | Statement | Page |
|---|---|---|---|
| LANG-03-01 | LR 3.2 | `;` outside strings, comments, raw template regions: parse error | [03](03-lexical.md) |
| LANG-03-02 | LR 3.2 | newline termination and continuation follow the 3.2 token lists exactly | [03](03-lexical.md) |
| LANG-03-03 | LR 3.3 | identifier category from its first character | [03](03-lexical.md) |
| LANG-03-04 | LR 3.4 | keywords reserved in declaration/binding positions; allowed as method/associated-function names and after `.` | [A](appendix-a-keywords.md) |
| LANG-03-05 | LR 3.5 | literal typing per 3.5; out-of-range literal rejected at compile time | [03](03-lexical.md) |
| LANG-03-06 | LR 3.6 | interpolations evaluated once, in order; never fallible or suspending | [03](03-lexical.md) |
| LANG-04-01 | LR 4.2 | module identity = file path; modules hold only declarations and constants | [04](04-modules.md) |
| LANG-04-02 | LR 4.2 | importing executes no code | [04](04-modules.md) |
| LANG-04-03 | LR 4.3 | only `exports:` modules importable across packages | [04](04-modules.md) |
| LANG-04-04 | LR 4.1 | distinct nominal types per package version and per module | [04](04-modules.md) |
| LANG-04-05 | LR 4.5 | shadowing a visible binding rejected | [04](04-modules.md) |
| LANG-04-06 | LR 4.6 | entry = the `main` of the manifest's entry module, exported or not, one of the four heads (each optionally `recovers`); each parameter `List[String]` or a capability type, each type once, supplied by its type | [04](04-modules.md) |
| LANG-05-01 | LR 5.1 | `let` declares, and its pattern matches every value; `=` assigns only a visible mutable target | [05](05-statements.md) |
| LANG-05-02 | LR 5.1 | block exit: end loans, run defers LIFO, drop locals in reverse initialisation order | [05](05-statements.md) |
| LANG-05-03 | LR 5.2 | `if`/`while` conditions are `Bool` | [05](05-statements.md) |
| LANG-05-04 | LR 5.3 | ranged `for` refines its index; index immutable | [05](05-statements.md) |
| LANG-05-05 | LR 5.4 | non-`Void` function ends every path in `return`, `fail` or `Never` | [05](05-statements.md) |
| LANG-05-06 | LR 5.6 | precedence per 5.6; mixed families without parentheses: parse error | [05](05-statements.md) |
| LANG-05-07 | LR 5.7 | evaluation order per 5.7, identical on both backends | [05](05-statements.md) |
| LANG-05-08 | LR 5.5, LR 12.3 | discarding a linear value rejected, except a never-polled future holding nothing linear and no exclusive loan; other non-`Void` values need `discard`, except a call statement of an `@ignorable` function | [05](05-statements.md) |
| LANG-05-09 | LR 5.8 | named after positional; each parameter once; names are exported signature; a pun `x` is `x: x` | [05](05-statements.md) |
| LANG-06-01 | LR 6.1, LR 6.9 | nominal identity survives calls, storage, serialisation, FFI | [06](06-types.md) |
| LANG-06-02 | LR 6.3 | structural refinement subtyping; interval domain exactly as listed | [06](06-types.md), [proofs](06-proofs.md) |
| LANG-06-03 | LR 6.3 | untrusted values pass the checked `as` conversion before holding a refined or nominal type | [06](06-types.md) |
| LANG-06-04 | LR 6.4, LR 6.5 | integer, `Decimal`, listed float operations bit-exact across VM and native; a checked operator fails as its function, at the same operation | [06](06-types.md) |
| LANG-06-05 | LR 6.5 | float operators total, strict IEEE; float refinements rejected | [06](06-types.md) |
| LANG-06-06 | LR 6.7 | `Map`/`Set` iteration deterministic per build | [06](06-types.md) |
| LANG-06-07 | LR 6.11 | trivial and copyable sets exactly as in 6.11 | [06](06-types.md) |
| LANG-06-08 | LR 6.8 | optional, `Bool`, `Outcome` never convert into one another | [06](06-types.md) |
| LANG-06-09 | LR 6.12 | linear values consumed exactly once | [06](06-types.md) |
| LANG-06-10 | LR 6.10, LR 9.5 | coherence: implementation in the package of the interface or the type; no overlap | [06](06-types.md) |
| LANG-06-11 | LR 6.10 | type arguments unfixed by arguments and expected type: rejected | [06](06-types.md) |
| LANG-06-12 | LR 6.10 | Associated calls on a type parameter are rejected; methods of its interface bounds are callable. | [06](06-types.md) |
| LANG-06-13 | LR 9.5 | An implement block targets a non-generic program class or enum. | [06](06-types.md) |
| LANG-06-14 | LR 6.13 | Each as resolves to one conversion; identity is rejected and a newtype unwrap stays in its declaring module. | [06](06-types.md) |
| LANG-06-15 | LR 6.13 | Conversions are declared or explicitly derived, with one conversion per pair and the stated ownership mode. | [06](06-types.md) |
| LANG-06-16 | LR 6.7, LR 6.8, LR 10.2 | Collection and optional/outcome callbacks obey their signature modes, effects and copying bounds on every backend. | [06](06-types.md) |

## LR 7-9

| Rule | LR | Statement | Page |
|---|---|---|---|
| LANG-07-01 | LR 7.5 | existing ownership-bearing place assigned/returned/captured carries `copy`/`alias`/`move`, except that returning a local `let` binding moves it; `owned`/`editable` arguments carry their marker; an unmarked `editable self` receiver or `fn mut` call checked as the marked one, rejected where the marker could not be written | [07](07-ownership.md) |
| LANG-07-02 | LR 7.6 | parameters never reassignable | [07](07-ownership.md) |
| LANG-07-03 | LR 7.10 | no inserted clones, reference counts or hidden sharing | [07](07-ownership.md), [C](appendix-c-lowering.md) |
| LANG-07-04 | LR 7.3, LR 7.4 | use after move, conflicting loans, loaned-owner use, escaping loans rejected, incl. closures, `defer`, `await`, `scope` | [07](07-ownership.md) |
| LANG-07-05 | LR 7.3 | loans lexical; aliasing invariant at every point | [07](07-ownership.md) |
| LANG-07-06 | LR 7.6, LR 7.7 | returned loans name one origin; lifetime parameter or loan-carrying field (not `from static`) rejected | [07](07-ownership.md) |
| LANG-07-07 | LR 7.9 | destruction order per 7.9 on both backends | [07](07-ownership.md) |
| LANG-07-08 | LR 7.8 | sharing explicit (`retain`); `copy` of `Shared` rejected | [07](07-ownership.md) |
| LANG-07-09 | LR 7.10 | unsupported shapes rejected, never lowered with `unsafe` or erasure | [C](appendix-c-lowering.md) |
| LANG-08-01 | LR 8.1 | parameter and success types stated (a head may leave out `Void`; a lambda's as 8.2 allows); modifiers in 8.1 order | [08](08-functions.md) |
| LANG-08-02 | LR 8.2, LR 8.3 | Written captures and kind, except inferred captures and kind on directly loaned literals. | [08](08-functions.md) |
| LANG-08-03 | LR 8.3 | Names outside the written or inferred capture list are inaccessible. | [08](08-functions.md) |
| LANG-08-04 | LR 8.4 | callable assignability per 8.4; no boxing without `dynamic fn` | [08](08-functions.md) |
| LANG-09-01 | LR 9.1 | no inheritance, runtime member lookup, reflection-based construction | [09](09-classes.md) |
| LANG-09-02 | LR 9.2 | generated constructor only where every field is visible | [09](09-classes.md) |
| LANG-09-03 | LR 9.5 | implementations never strengthen preconditions or weaken guarantees; coherence | [09](09-classes.md) |
| LANG-09-04 | LR 9.6 | Mixins require methods only; compatible signatures, bodies checked at each application, no state, no unresolved conflicts. | [09](09-classes.md) |
| LANG-09-05 | LR 9.8 | closed-type `match` exhaustive without `otherwise`; each missing variant named; or-pattern alternatives count, bind nothing, take no guard | [09](09-classes.md) |
| LANG-09-06 | LR 9.8 | pattern binding ownership per 9.8 | [09](09-classes.md) |
| LANG-09-07 | LR 9.5 | `dynamic I` requires dynamic eligibility and an implementing source type. | [09](09-classes.md) |

## LR 10-14

| Rule | LR | Statement | Page |
|---|---|---|---|
| LANG-10-01 | LR 10.1, LR 10.2 | outcomes wrapped until consumed by a 10.2 operation | [10](10-outcomes.md) |
| LANG-10-02 | LR 10.7 | obligations survive collections, fields, closures; dropping rejected | [10](10-outcomes.md) |
| LANG-10-03 | LR 10.6 | reported failure unreachable afterwards; `annotate` keeps one obligation | [10](10-outcomes.md) |
| LANG-10-04 | LR 10.3 | `noalloc try` uses the bounded failure representation | [10](10-outcomes.md) |
| LANG-10-05 | LR 10.4 | `recover` without a prior `report` adds `recovers` | [10](10-outcomes.md) |
| LANG-10-06 | LR 10.8 | defects follow the 10.8 taxonomy; never catchable | [10](10-outcomes.md) |
| LANG-11-01 | LR 11.1, LR 11.3 | exactly eight effects; transitive fixed-point summaries | [11](11-effects.md) |
| LANG-11-02 | LR 11.1, LR 11.3 | fresh-storage and own-`editable`-parameter writes are not `mutate`; captures, guards, atomics are | [11](11-effects.md) |
| LANG-11-03 | LR 11.4 | `noalloc` against the whitelist for the target and telemetry plan | [11](11-effects.md), [C](appendix-c-lowering.md) |
| LANG-11-04 | LR 11.3 | trusted summaries labelled `trusted`, never `proved` | [11](11-effects.md) |
| LANG-11-05 | LR 11.3 | `async`/`try`/`recovers` written; only written `pure`/`noalloc` cross modules; weakening exported modifiers reported | [11](11-effects.md) |
| LANG-11-06 | LR 11.5, LR 11.6 | Contracts contain only the listed elements; contradictions are rejected and capability clauses name Authority types. | [11](11-effects.md) |
| LANG-11-07 | LR 11.6 | `io` (except `report` and the `log` statements) needs an `Authority`; only the entry `main` receives capabilities, as parameters, or creates them once with `Host.capabilities()` when it declares none; every other use of `Host.capabilities` and every reference to the entry `main` rejected | [11](11-effects.md) |
| LANG-11-08 | LR 11.5, LR 11.8 | contracts in modifier position, no arguments; `@` for aspects only | [11](11-effects.md) |
| LANG-11-09 | LR 11.8 | aspects have only the 11.8 parts, elaborate before checking, pass every check | [11](11-effects.md) |
| LANG-12-01 | LR 12.1 | `defer` checked at every exit; cannot alter the outcome; named places initialised at every exit | [12](12-async.md) |
| LANG-12-02 | LR 12.1 | failures in `defer` consumed there; never replace the primary outcome | [12](12-async.md) |
| LANG-12-03 | LR 12.3, LR 12.4 | `Future`/`Task` linear; pending future never destroyed; cancellation only at cancellation points | [12](12-async.md) |
| LANG-12-04 | LR 12.5 | a scope joins or cancels every task before its block exits | [12](12-async.md) |
| LANG-12-05 | LR 12.5, LR 12.7 | only `Shareable` environments cross pools; loans cross only cooperative `launch` | [12](12-async.md) |
| LANG-12-06 | LR 12.3, LR 12.7 | no `MutexGuard` live across `await` | [12](12-async.md) |
| LANG-13-01 | LR 13 | `capture` snapshots a pure, infallible expression | [13](13-observation.md) |
| LANG-13-02 | LR 13 | required fields assigned exactly once per applicable exit; loops and doubles rejected | [13](13-observation.md) |
| LANG-13-03 | LR 13 | frames bounded by the schema; truncation or omission recorded | [13](13-observation.md) |
| LANG-13-04 | LR 13 | each `log.info`/`log.warn`/`log.error` writes exactly one `log` record to the diagnostic plane, never standard output, the same on every backend; needs no `Authority`; has the `io` effect | [13](13-observation.md) |
| LANG-14-01 | LR 14 | table rows bound with `as` | [14](14-tests.md) |
| LANG-14-02 | LR 14 | `expect` takes `Bool`, records typed evidence | [14](14-tests.md) |
| LANG-14-03 | LR 14, LR 6.4 | in `test`/`property` bodies a fallible call nothing else consumes (`or`, `catch`, `match`, a `let` later consumed as an outcome or annotated `Outcome[…]`), and unproved `Int` arithmetic, behave as followed by `or fail`; outside them nothing changes | [14](14-tests.md) |
| LANG-14-04 | LR 14 | `expect` is valid only in test, property and cases bodies. | [14](14-tests.md) |

|---|---|---|

# Glossary (agent mode)

<!-- covers: LR E -->
*Agent mode. Human mode: [Glossary](../guide/glossary.md).*

One meaning per term; where a word has two meanings both rows are listed. A bundle of packages is a kit.
The Language Reference's glossary is LR E; this page adds the in-language terms.

## System

| Term | Definition | Source |
|---|---|---|
| package | unit of distribution, versioning, visibility: `project.yaml`, lockfile, `src/`; two versions are two packages | LR 4.1 |
| module | one `.ft` file under `src/`; name = path below `src/` with `.` separators; declarations and constants only | LR 4.2 |
| kit | named, versioned bundle of packages shipped with the distribution; extends Fortis only by libraries, aspects, heads, embedding bindings, verifiers; never changes core semantics | LR 16 |
| compatibility set | the standard packages at the versions tested together; a standard dependency names the set's version | LR 4.1 |
| toolchain component | daemon, LSP, SDK generators: tools, not kits | LR 16 |
| backend | interpreter (`fortis run`, the reference), development VM (`fortisc vm`), native (`fortis build`); must agree | LR 1 |
| build mode | `dev` (VM), `native-dev`, `release`; optimisation and debug settings belong to a mode | LR 1 |
| lint level | baseline (an unused import warns) or strict (it is an error) | LR 4.3 |
| target feature set | which standard modules exist for a target (`core`, `alloc`, `host`, `async`, `web`, `browser`) | LR 11.6 |

## Declarations

| Term | Definition | Source |
|---|---|---|
| head (declaration head) | reserved keyword introducing a schema-validated declaration elaborated to core declarations before type checking; owner: the core (`observation`, LR 13), developer tooling (`explore`, LR E), or a kit (the rest) | LR 16, LR 13, LR E |
| elaboration | rewriting a head, or a function with aspects, into core declarations before ownership and effect checking | LR 16, LR 11.8 |
| extension slot | head block; `inject` member; aspect application; `cases` table: the only four | LR 16 |
| raw template region | text of `view { … }` in a head body, handed unlexed to the Web UI kit | LR 16 |
| aspect | `@name(args)` behaviour around a function: `needs`, `before`, `after`, `on failure`, `metadata`; adds | LR 11.8 |
| contract | named conjunction of modifiers, forbidden effects, required or excluded authorities; subtracts | LR 11.5 |
| mixin | methods applied with `with`; requires methods, adds no state | LR 9.6 |
| newtype | `type Name = Repr`; nominal, private representation | LR 6.9 |
| refinement | predicate in `<…>` on a built-in type | LR 6.3 |
| binding (name) | name introduced by `let`, `let mut`, a parameter, a pattern or a capture | LR 5.1, LR 7.2 |
| binding (embedded language) | versioned package giving a language fenced blocks via the embedding protocol; meaning compiler-fixed, checking a verifier (SP-23, not yet in the LR) | [Embedded languages](embedded-languages.md) |
| verifier | stricter-only package: reads the checked program, returns records never code; pure, deterministic, bounded, no capability | [Embedded languages](embedded-languages.md) |

## Ownership

| Term | Definition | Source |
|---|---|---|
| place | binding; field path rooted in a binding or `self`; `Array` element with a literal index | LR 7.2 |
| owner | binding holding a value until it is moved out | LR 7.2 |
| loan | `alias` (read) or `editable` (exclusive) reference to a place; lexical | LR 7.3 |
| child loan | a loan taken through a loan-holding binding, recorded against the owner | LR 7.3 |
| marker | `copy`, `alias`, `move`, `editable` before a place; left out where the declaration already shows it (an `editable self` receiver on a `let mut` root, `return local`) | LR 7.5 |
| loan-carrying value | standard views and cursors; store a read loan; owned by their binding | LR 7.7 |
| trivial | duplicated implicitly, never marked | LR 6.11 |
| copyable | supports `copy` | LR 6.11 |
| linear | consumed exactly once on every path | LR 6.12 |
| shareable | may cross `launchParallel` / `launchBlocking` | LR 12.7 |

## Failures, effects, authority

| Term | Definition | Source |
|---|---|---|
| outcome | `Outcome[T]` from a `try` function; linear | LR 10.1 |
| checked region | `Int` arithmetic as the left operand of `or fail`/`or recover`/`catch`; an unproved operator in it is the checked operation | LR 6.4 |
| failure | `Failure`: code, payload, origin, cause chain; linear | LR 10.3 |
| obligation | the duty to consume a linear value | LR 7.1, LR 10.1 |
| defect | broken-assumption condition (stack, memory, trusted contract, runtime invariant); never caught | LR 10.8 |
| effect | one of `alloc`, `io`, `mutate`, `nondet`, `suspend`, `block`, `fail`, `recovers` | LR 11.1 |
| effect summary | a function's effect subset, computed transitively | LR 11.1, LR 11.3 |
| write footprint | `editable` parameters a function writes through | LR 11.3 |
| fresh storage | created in this activation, not yet reachable from a parameter, capture or `self` | LR 11.1 |
| authority | value implementing `Authority`; required for `io` | LR 11.6 |
| capability | process-wide authority (ten types), supplied to the entry `main`'s parameters by type | LR 11.6, LR 4.6 |
| per-activation authority | minted by a kit adapter from a capability for one unit of work | LR 11.6 |
| trusted | bodiless standard intrinsic; claims reported as trusted, never proved | LR 11.3 |

## Concurrency and observation

| Term | Definition | Source |
|---|---|---|
| scope | `scope name { … }`: owns tasks; joins or cancels them before exit | LR 12.5 |
| task | `Task[T]` from a launch; linear | LR 12.5 |
| cancellation point | `await`; on the pools also `checkpoint()` | LR 12.4 |
| observation schema | `observation` declaration of typed frame fields | LR 13 |
| observation frame | one activation's captured fields | LR 13 |
| event | one `record` execution | LR 13 |
| task reporter | diagnostic-plane sink for reports, logs and frames | LR 15 |
| log record | one `log.info`/`log.warn`/`log.error` execution: level, message, function; standard error, never standard output | LR 13 |
| diagnostic plane | output channel nothing can read back | LR 11.7 |
| record (tool output) | schema-valid object; text on a terminal, JSON line otherwise | [records](records.md) |

source: docs/agent/worked-example.md

# Coffee shop: checked domain model

<!-- covers: LR 6, LR 8, LR 9, LR 10, LR 11.5, LR 14 -->
*Agent mode. Human mode: [Model a domain](../guide/worked-example.md). Source of truth: LR 6, LR 8, LR 9,
LR 10, LR 11.5 and LR 14.*

The complete [v0.1.0 showcase](../../examples/showcase/v0.1.0-coffee.ft) and its
[expected stdout](../../examples/showcase/v0.1.0-coffee.stdout) are pinned. The gate checks both checkers and
runs `main` and tests on all three backends. The guide contains the same complete program, also checked by docset.

## Construction order and rules

| Step | Program shape | Rule and constraint |
|---|---|---|
| Model | `Pence`, `Size`, `Drink.quantity` | LANG-06-01/02/03: nominal newtype, const refinement bound, proved constructor; private unwrap with `as` (LR 6.3, LR 6.9, LR 6.13). |
| Behaviour | `Priced`, `Labelled`, `Pricing` | LANG-09-03/04/07, LANG-11-06: compatible interface methods, mixin method requirements, dynamic eligibility, consistent effect contract (LR 9.5, LR 9.6, LR 11.5). |
| Parse | enum derive and `Drink` conversion | LANG-06-14/15: ASCII case-insensitive enum names; trim separately; split, parse and refine; every fallible `as` handled (LR 6.6, LR 6.13). |
| Collect | loop over `orders.lines()` | LANG-10-01/03: move each success into `Basket`, report each failure; collection-newtype editing private to this module (LR 6.9, LR 10.2, LR 10.6). |
| Summarise | `each`, `fold`, searches, sorting, grouping | LANG-06-16, LANG-08-02/04: inferred captures only for directly loaned literals; exact callback modes and declared effects; copying methods require Copyable (LR 6.7, LR 8.2, LR 8.4, LR 11.3). |
| Fail early | `tryMap`, `tryEach`, `tryFold` | Outcome-returning callbacks, stop on first failure, handle the result (LR 6.7, LR 10.2). |
| Reuse | `Ticket`, `Pastry`, `larger`, `Pending` | Explicit field-wise conversion; implement block; Comparable and Copyable bounds; `where T: linear` and transfer of the owned obligation (LR 6.10, LR 6.12, LR 6.13, LR 9.5, LR 10.7). |
| Containers | `Deque`, `SortedSet`, `Array`, `Map`, `Set` | Import the first two; Array view borrows; hash keys need Hashable and Equatable; no stored loan outlives its owner (LR 6.7, LR 7.7). |
| Test | example, cases, property | LANG-14-04: `expect` only in test code; refine generated quantities by their type (LR 14). |

A declared `convert from String` member accepts literals and `StringView` sources as read loans; an `owned String`
parameter copies those sources (LR 6.13). Property tests run today, with their full release scope still v0.2.

## Verification

<!-- no-citation: tool commands and the showcase gate, not language rules -->

```sh
python3 -I conformance/tools/gate.py --only showcase
bin/fortis check examples/showcase/v0.1.0-coffee.ft --format json
bin/fortis test examples/showcase/v0.1.0-coffee.ft
compiler/target/release/fortisc test examples/showcase/v0.1.0-coffee.ft
compiler/target/release/fortisc native examples/showcase/v0.1.0-coffee.ft --tests
```

Read diagnostics before changing the source: [codes and corrections](codes.md). Do not change the expected
output or remove assertions to make a backend pass.

source: docs/agent/library.md

# The core library

<!-- covers: LR 15 -->
*Agent mode. Human mode: [The core library](../guide/library.md). Generated by `conformance/tools/libref.py` from the declarations
of `library/fortis` and the effect data of `reference/library/effects`; do not edit.
Source of truth: LR 15 for the inventory, and each declaration's own contract.*

> Preview: the core runtime inventory (LR 15) arrives in v0.4.

Every public declaration of the seven core modules (LR 15): each exported declaration, every member of an
exported interface (whose members share its visibility, LR 4.4) and every variant of an exported enum, with its
signature as the library declares it, the effects it declares and the contract its documentation comment
states. The check counts these against the module sources independently of this page. A `trusted` operation is
implemented by the toolchain, and its comment is its review record (LR 11.3). `fortis.prelude` is imported into
every module; the other modules need an `import` (LR 4.3). What is not listed here does not exist in Language
1.0's core library; the gaps against the Language Reference are recorded as D-58.

The Effects column is `pure` or `noalloc` where the signature claims it, then the effects the operation has,
which a caller inherits (LR 11.1, 11.3): `alloc`, `fail` (a `try` function), `suspend` (`async`), `recovers`,
`block`, `io` (a capability's method, or an operation that takes an authority), `mutate`, `nondet`, and
`writes self` (an impure `editable self` method). `none` is an impure operation with no effect to declare; a
type has none.

## `fortis.prelude`

Imported into every module: the built-in types, the optional and outcome operations, the built-in interfaces (LR 4.3, LR 6.2, LR 6.10).

### `class Void`

### `class Never`

### `class Bool`

### `class Int`

| Declaration | Effects | Contract |
|---|---|---|
| `trusted pure try func add(a: Int, b: Int) Int` | pure; fail | checked 64-bit two's-complement addition; fails `numeric.overflow` outside [-2^63, 2^63-1]; O(1), no allocation |
| `trusted pure try func sub(a: Int, b: Int) Int` | pure; fail | checked subtraction; fails `numeric.overflow`; O(1), no allocation |
| `trusted pure try func mul(a: Int, b: Int) Int` | pure; fail | checked multiplication; fails `numeric.overflow`; O(1), no allocation |
| `trusted pure try func div(a: Int, b: Int) Int` | pure; fail | truncating division; fails `numeric.divide_by_zero` when b = 0 and `numeric.overflow` for -2^63 / -1; O(1) |
| `trusted pure try func rem(a: Int, b: Int) Int` | pure; fail | remainder with the sign of a; fails `numeric.divide_by_zero` when b = 0; O(1) |
| `trusted pure try func shiftLeft(a: Int, bits: Int) Int` | pure; fail | a * 2^bits; fails `numeric.shift_range` unless 0 <= bits < 64 and `numeric.overflow` when the result is out of range; O(1) |
| `trusted pure func wrappingAdd(a: Int, b: Int) Int` | pure | addition modulo 2^64 into [-2^63, 2^63-1]; total; O(1) |
| `trusted pure func wrappingSub(a: Int, b: Int) Int` | pure | subtraction modulo 2^64; total; O(1) |
| `trusted pure func wrappingMul(a: Int, b: Int) Int` | pure | multiplication modulo 2^64; total; O(1) |
| `trusted pure func saturatingAdd(a: Int, b: Int) Int` | pure | addition clamped to [-2^63, 2^63-1]; total; O(1) |
| `trusted pure func saturatingSub(a: Int, b: Int) Int` | pure | subtraction clamped to [-2^63, 2^63-1]; total; O(1) |
| `trusted pure func saturatingMul(a: Int, b: Int) Int` | pure | multiplication clamped to [-2^63, 2^63-1]; total; O(1) |
| `trusted pure try func validate(value: Int) Int` | pure; fail | the value when it lies in the refinement of the receiver type; fails `refinement.out_of_range` otherwise; O(1) |

| `trusted pure func totalOrder(x: Float) Int64` | pure | the IEEE 754 totalOrder key of x as a signed 64-bit integer; O(1) |
| `trusted pure func bitsEqual(a: Float, b: Float) Bool` | pure | true exactly when a and b have the same 64-bit pattern; O(1) |
| `trusted pure func isNaN(x: Float) Bool` | pure | true exactly for NaN; O(1) |

### `enum RoundingMode`

Variants: `HalfEven`, `HalfAwayFromZero`, `TowardZero`, `AwayFromZero`.

### `class Decimal`

| Declaration | Effects | Contract |
|---|---|---|
| `trusted pure try func add(a: Decimal, b: Decimal) Decimal` | pure; fail | the sum at the larger operand scale, rounded half to even when it needs more than 96 coefficient bits; fails `numeric.overflow` when the integer part does not fit (6.4); O(digits) |
| `trusted pure try func sub(a: Decimal, b: Decimal) Decimal` | pure; fail | the difference at the larger operand scale, rounded half to even when needed; fails `numeric.overflow` (6.4); O(digits) |
| `trusted pure try func mul(a: Decimal, b: Decimal) Decimal` | pure; fail | the product at the sum of the scales, rounded half to even above 28 fractional digits or 96 coefficient bits; fails `numeric.overflow` (6.4); O(digits^2) |
| `trusted pure try func div(a: Decimal, b: Decimal) Decimal` | pure; fail | the quotient at the largest scale that fits, rounded half to even; fails `numeric.divide_by_zero` and `numeric.overflow` (6.4); O(digits^2) |
| `trusted pure try func rem(a: Decimal, b: Decimal) Decimal` | pure; fail | the remainder with the sign of the dividend at the larger operand scale; fails `numeric.divide_by_zero` (6.4); O(digits^2) |
| `trusted pure func round(value: Decimal, scale: Int<0..28>, mode: RoundingMode) Decimal` | pure | value rounded to scale by mode; total; O(digits) |
| `trusted pure try func fromFloat(x: Float, scale: Int<0..28>, mode: RoundingMode) Decimal` | pure; fail | the binary value of x rounded to scale by mode; fails `numeric.overflow` for a non-finite x or an integer part that does not fit (6.4); O(digits) |
| `trusted pure func scale(self) Int<0..28>` | pure | the number of fractional digits; O(1) |

### `class BigInt`

### `class String`

| Declaration | Effects | Contract |
|---|---|---|
| `trusted pure func from(text: StringView) String` | pure; alloc | an owned copy of the view; allocates; O(n) in bytes |
| `pure func empty() String` | pure | — |
| `trusted pure func scalarCount(self) Int` | pure | the number of Unicode scalar values; O(n) in bytes |
| `trusted pure func byteCount(self) Int` | pure | the UTF-8 length in bytes; O(1) |
| `trusted pure func trim(self) StringView from self` | pure | the view without its leading and trailing Unicode White_Space (U+0009 to U+000D, U+0020, U+0085, U+00A0, U+1680, U+2000 to U+200A, U+2028, U+2029, U+202F, U+205F, U+3000) scalars; a view of the same text, no allocation; O(n) in bytes |
| `trusted pure func trimStart(self) StringView from self` | pure | the view without its leading White_Space scalars (as trim); a view of the same text, no allocation; O(n) in bytes |
| `trusted pure func trimEnd(self) StringView from self` | pure | the view without its trailing White_Space scalars (as trim); a view of the same text, no allocation; O(n) in bytes |
| `trusted pure func find(self, needle: StringView) Int<0..>?` | pure | the scalar offset (the unit of slice and scalarAt) of the first occurrence of needle, null when it does not occur; an empty needle occurs at 0; no allocation; at most O(n * m) in bytes for a text of n bytes and a needle of m |
| `pure func contains(self, needle: StringView) Bool` | pure | true exactly when find(needle) is present: an empty needle is contained in every text |
| `trusted pure func startsWith(self, prefix: StringView) Bool` | pure | true exactly when the text begins with prefix (an empty prefix always does); no allocation; O(m) in bytes for a prefix of m |
| `trusted pure func endsWith(self, suffix: StringView) Bool` | pure | true exactly when the text ends with suffix (an empty suffix always does); no allocation; O(m) in bytes for a suffix of m |
| `trusted pure func split(self, separator: StringView) List[String]` | pure; alloc | the pieces between the non-overlapping occurrences of separator, found left to right, as owned strings; a separator at either end gives an empty piece there, a text without the separator gives one piece (itself), and an empty separator occurs nowhere, so it gives one piece; allocates; O(n) in bytes |
| `trusted pure func lines(self) List[String]` | pure; alloc | the lines of the text as owned strings, each ended by a line feed or by a carriage return and a line feed (neither stays in the line); the text after the last terminator is a line only when it is not empty, so "" has no lines and "a\n" has one; a carriage return not before a line feed stays in the line; allocates; O(n) in bytes |
| `trusted pure func replace(self, old: StringView, new: StringView) String` | pure; alloc | a copy of the text with every non-overlapping occurrence of old, found left to right, replaced by new; an empty old occurs nowhere, so the copy is unchanged; allocates; O(n) in bytes plus the find cost |
| `trusted pure func asciiUpper(self) String` | pure; alloc | a copy with the ASCII letters a-z mapped to A-Z and every other scalar unchanged (not Unicode case mapping: that depends on the Unicode version and the language, and changes lengths); allocates; O(n) in bytes |
| `trusted pure func asciiLower(self) String` | pure; alloc | a copy with the ASCII letters A-Z mapped to a-z and every other scalar unchanged (as asciiUpper); allocates; O(n) in bytes |
| `pure func repeat(self, times: Int<0..>) String` | pure; alloc | the text written times in a row: "" when times is 0 or the text is empty; allocates; O(times * n) in bytes |
| `pure func join(parts: ListView[String], separator: StringView) String` | pure; alloc | the parts in order with separator between neighbours: "" for no parts and the part itself for one; allocates; O(total length) |

### `class StringView`

| Declaration | Effects | Contract |
|---|---|---|
| `trusted pure func scalarCount(self) Int` | pure | the number of Unicode scalar values; O(n) in bytes |
| `trusted pure func byteCount(self) Int` | pure | the UTF-8 length in bytes; O(1) |
| `trusted pure try func slice(self, start: Int, end: Int) StringView` | pure; fail | the scalars [start, end) as a view of the same owner; fails `text.slice_bounds` unless 0 <= start <= end <= scalarCount; O(n) in bytes, no allocation |
| `trusted pure try func scalarAt(self, index: Int) Scalar` | pure; fail | the scalar at index; fails `text.index` past the end; O(n) in bytes |
| `trusted pure func trim(self) StringView from self` | pure | the view without its leading and trailing Unicode White_Space (U+0009 to U+000D, U+0020, U+0085, U+00A0, U+1680, U+2000 to U+200A, U+2028, U+2029, U+202F, U+205F, U+3000) scalars; a view of the same text, no allocation; O(n) in bytes |
| `trusted pure func trimStart(self) StringView from self` | pure | the view without its leading White_Space scalars (as trim); a view of the same text, no allocation; O(n) in bytes |
| `trusted pure func trimEnd(self) StringView from self` | pure | the view without its trailing White_Space scalars (as trim); a view of the same text, no allocation; O(n) in bytes |
| `trusted pure func find(self, needle: StringView) Int<0..>?` | pure | the scalar offset (the unit of slice and scalarAt) of the first occurrence of needle, null when it does not occur; an empty needle occurs at 0; no allocation; at most O(n * m) in bytes for a text of n bytes and a needle of m |
| `pure func contains(self, needle: StringView) Bool` | pure | true exactly when find(needle) is present: an empty needle is contained in every text |
| `trusted pure func startsWith(self, prefix: StringView) Bool` | pure | true exactly when the text begins with prefix (an empty prefix always does); no allocation; O(m) in bytes for a prefix of m |
| `trusted pure func endsWith(self, suffix: StringView) Bool` | pure | true exactly when the text ends with suffix (an empty suffix always does); no allocation; O(m) in bytes for a suffix of m |
| `trusted pure func split(self, separator: StringView) List[String]` | pure; alloc | the pieces between the non-overlapping occurrences of separator, found left to right, as owned strings; a separator at either end gives an empty piece there, a text without the separator gives one piece (itself), and an empty separator occurs nowhere, so it gives one piece; allocates; O(n) in bytes |
| `trusted pure func lines(self) List[String]` | pure; alloc | the lines of the text as owned strings, each ended by a line feed or by a carriage return and a line feed (neither stays in the line); the text after the last terminator is a line only when it is not empty, so "" has no lines and "a\n" has one; a carriage return not before a line feed stays in the line; allocates; O(n) in bytes |
| `trusted pure func replace(self, old: StringView, new: StringView) String` | pure; alloc | a copy of the text with every non-overlapping occurrence of old, found left to right, replaced by new; an empty old occurs nowhere, so the copy is unchanged; allocates; O(n) in bytes plus the find cost |
| `trusted pure func asciiUpper(self) String` | pure; alloc | a copy with the ASCII letters a-z mapped to A-Z and every other scalar unchanged (not Unicode case mapping: that depends on the Unicode version and the language, and changes lengths); allocates; O(n) in bytes |
| `trusted pure func asciiLower(self) String` | pure; alloc | a copy with the ASCII letters A-Z mapped to a-z and every other scalar unchanged (as asciiUpper); allocates; O(n) in bytes |
| `pure func repeat(self, times: Int<0..>) String` | pure; alloc | the text written times in a row: "" when times is 0 or the text is empty; allocates; O(times * n) in bytes |

### `class Duration`

| Declaration | Effects | Contract |
|---|---|---|
| `trusted pure func days(n: Int<0..>) Duration` | pure | n * 86400 * 10^9 nanoseconds; O(1) (n bounded by the 64-bit count) |
| `trusted pure func hours(n: Int<0..>) Duration` | pure | n * 3600 * 10^9 nanoseconds; O(1) |
| `trusted pure func minutes(n: Int<0..>) Duration` | pure | n * 60 * 10^9 nanoseconds; O(1) |
| `trusted pure func seconds(n: Int<0..>) Duration` | pure | n * 10^9 nanoseconds; O(1) |
| `trusted pure func milliseconds(n: Int<0..>) Duration` | pure | n * 10^6 nanoseconds; O(1) |
| `trusted pure try func add(a: Duration, b: Duration) Duration` | pure; fail | sum of the signed 64-bit nanosecond counts; fails `numeric.overflow`; O(1) |
| `trusted pure try func sub(a: Duration, b: Duration) Duration` | pure; fail | difference of the nanosecond counts; fails `numeric.overflow`; O(1) |
| `trusted pure try func multiply(d: Duration, factor: Int) Duration` | pure; fail | the count times factor; fails `numeric.overflow`; O(1) |
| `trusted pure func nanoseconds(self) Int` | pure | the signed 64-bit nanosecond count; O(1) |

### `class List[T]`

| Declaration | Effects | Contract |
|---|---|---|
| `trusted pure func default() List[T]` | pure | an empty list with no allocation until the first push; O(1) |
| `trusted pure func of(...items: owned T) List[T]` | pure; alloc | a list holding the arguments in order; allocates once; O(n) |
| `trusted pure func count(self) Int` | pure | the number of elements; O(1) |
| `trusted func push(editable self, item: owned T)` | alloc, writes self | appends item; amortised O(1) (capacity doubles), worst case O(n) for the growth step |
| `trusted func pop(editable self) T?` | writes self | removes and returns the last element, null when empty; O(1) |
| `trusted pure func get(self, index: Int) (alias T from self)?` | pure | a read loan of the element at index, null outside [0, count); O(1) |
| `trusted pure try func at(self, index: Int) T` | pure; fail | the element at index; fails `collection.index` outside [0, count); O(1) |
| `trusted try func set(editable self, index: Int, value: owned T)` | fail, writes self | replaces the element at index, dropping the old value; fails `collection.index`; O(1) |
| `trusted func clear(editable self)` | writes self | removes and drops every element; rejected for a linear element type (10.7): consume them instead; O(n) |
| `pure func isEmpty(self) Bool` | pure | — |
| `pure func first(self) (alias T from self)?` | pure | — |
| `pure func reversed(self) List[T] where T implements Copyable` | pure; alloc | — |
| `pure func concat(self, other: ListView[T]) List[T] where T implements Copyable` | pure; alloc | — |
| `pure func countWhere(self, keep: pure fn(T) Bool) Int` | pure | — |
| `pure func map[U](self, f: pure fn(T) U) List[U] where U: linear` | pure; alloc | — |
| `pure func filter(self, keep: pure fn(T) Bool) List[T] where T implements Copyable` | pure; alloc | — |
| `func each(self, visit: editable fn mut(T) Void)` | none | calls visit with a read loan of every element in order (X-479); the callback may have effects, so `each` is not pure; O(n) plus the callback per element |
| `try func tryEach(self, visit: editable fn mut(T) Outcome[Void])` | fail | as `each`, stopping at the first failure of the callback and returning it (X-479); O(n) plus the callback per element |
| `pure try func tryMap[U](self, f: pure fn(T) Outcome[U]) List[U]` | pure; alloc, fail | as `map`, stopping at the first failure of the callback and returning it, with the new list dropped (X-479); allocates; O(n) plus the callback per element U must be non-linear: failure drops earlier results (10.7, E-OBL-003). (E-OBL-003: LR 5.3) |
| `pure func fold[A](self, initial: owned A, step: pure fn(A, T) A) A` | pure | step gets a read loan of the accumulator and an element, once per element in order, and returns the next accumulator (X-479); O(n) plus the callback per element |
| `pure try func tryFold[A](self, initial: owned A, step: pure fn(A, T) Outcome[A]) A` | pure; fail | as `fold`, stopping at the first failure of step and returning it (X-479); O(n) plus the callback per element |
| `pure func any(self, holds: pure fn(T) Bool) Bool` | pure | whether holds is true for some element; stops at the first one that passes (X-479); O(n) plus the callback |
| `pure func all(self, holds: pure fn(T) Bool) Bool` | pure | whether holds is true for every element; stops at the first one that fails (X-479); O(n) plus the callback |
| `pure func find(self, holds: pure fn(T) Bool) (alias T from self)?` | pure | a read loan of the first element holds is true for, null when none does (X-479); O(n) plus the callback |
| `pure func indexWhere(self, holds: pure fn(T) Bool) Int?` | pure | the index of the first element holds is true for, null when none does (X-479); O(n) plus the callback |
| `pure func contains(self, target: T) Bool where T implements Equatable` | pure | whether some element equals target (X-479); O(n) |
| `pure func enumerate(self) List[(Int, T)] where T implements Copyable` | pure; alloc | each element copied with its index, in order (X-479); allocates; O(n) |
| `pure func zip[U](self, other: ListView[U]) List[(T, U)] where T implements Copyable, U implements Copyable` | pure; alloc | pairs of copies of the elements at the same index of self and other, as many as the shorter has (X-479); allocates; O(min(n, m)) |
| `pure func take(self, n: Int) List[T] where T implements Copyable` | pure; alloc | copies of the first n elements, all of them when n is at least count(), none when n is 0 or less (X-479); allocates; O(min(n, count)) |
| `pure func skip(self, n: Int) List[T] where T implements Copyable` | pure; alloc | copies of the elements after the first n, none when n is at least count(), all when n is 0 or less (X-479); allocates; O(count) |
| `pure func flatMap[U](self, f: pure fn(T) List[U]) List[U] where U: linear` | pure; alloc | the lists f returns for each element, joined in order (X-479); allocates; O(n) plus the sizes of the lists plus the callback per element |
| `pure func chunked(self, size: Int<1..>) List[List[T]] where T implements Copyable` | pure; alloc | copies of the elements in lists of size elements, the last one shorter when size does not divide count() (X-479); allocates; O(n) |
| `pure func sortedBy[K](self, key: pure fn(T) K) List[T] where T implements Copyable, K implements Comparable` | pure; alloc | copies of the elements ordered by key(element), smaller keys first, elements with equal keys in their original order (a stable merge sort over indexes); key is called once per element (X-479); allocates; O(n log n) comparisons plus n callbacks |
| `pure func groupBy[K](self, key: pure fn(T) K) Map[K, List[T]] where T implements Copyable, K implements Copyable, K implements Hashable, K implements Equatable` | pure; alloc | copies of the elements gathered by key(element) into a Map from each key to its elements in their original order; the keys are in the order they first appear (X-479); allocates; expected O(n) plus n callbacks |
| `trusted pure func iterate(self) ListCursor[T] from self` | pure | a cursor over read loans of the elements in order; O(1) to create, O(1) per step |
| `trusted func consumeEach(owned self, visit: fn mut(owned T) Void)` | none | consumes the list (10.7): no early exit, so no element is left unvisited; an empty list makes no calls intrinsic: calls visit once per element in order, transferring each element out; O(n) plus the callback per element |

| `trusted func set(editable self, key: owned K, value: owned V)` | alloc, writes self | inserts or replaces the value for key, dropping a replaced value; amortised expected O(1) |
| `trusted pure func count(self) Int` | pure | the number of keys; O(1) |
| `trusted pure func containsKey(self, key: K) Bool` | pure | whether key has an entry (a StringView key on a Map[String, V], as `get`); expected O(1) |
| `trusted func remove(editable self, key: K) V?` | writes self | removes the entry for key and returns its value, which the caller now owns; null when there is none. The entries after it keep their order and move up one place, so the cost is O(n) in the entries after it (a StringView key on a Map[String, V], as `get`) |
| `pure func isEmpty(self) Bool where K implements Hashable` | pure | — |
| `func each(self, visit: editable fn mut(K, V) Void) where K implements Hashable` | none | calls visit with a read loan of every key and its value in first-insertion order (X-479); the callback may have effects, so `each` is not pure; O(n) plus the callback per entry |

| `pure func values(self) List[V] where K implements Hashable, V implements Copyable` | pure; alloc | copies of the values in first-insertion order (X-479); allocates; O(n) |

### `class Optional`

`Optional` is not a type a program names: it holds the helpers of a `T?` receiver, so `maybe.map(f)` is `Optional.map(maybe, f)`.

| Declaration | Effects | Contract |
|---|---|---|
| `pure func map[T, U](value: T?, f: pure fn(T) U) U? where U: linear` | pure | the present value is lent to f and f's result is the present result; null stays null and f is not called (X-479); O(1) plus the callback |

### `class Outcome[T]`

| Declaration | Effects | Contract |
|---|---|---|
| `trusted pure func success(value: owned T) Outcome[T]` | pure | an outcome holding value; O(1) |

| `trusted pure try func collect(list: owned List[Outcome[T]]) List[T]` | pure; alloc, fail | the successes in order when every element succeeds, otherwise the first failure in order, consuming every other element's obligation; T must be non-linear (10.7, E-OBL-003); O(n) (E-OBL-003: LR 5.3) |
| `pure func map[U](owned self, f: pure fn(T) U) Outcome[U] where U: linear` | pure | consumes the outcome; a success becomes the success of f applied to a read loan of its value, a failure passes through unchanged and f is not called (X-479); O(1) plus the callback T must be non-linear: the callback borrows a payload that is then dropped (10.7, E-OBL-003). (E-OBL-003: LR 5.3) |

### `class Mutex[T]`

| Declaration | Effects | Contract |
|---|---|---|
| `trusted pure func create(value: owned T) Mutex[T]` | pure | a mutex owning value; O(1) |
| `trusted async try func lock(self) MutexGuard[T] from self` | fail, suspend | an exclusive guard over the value, released when the guard is dropped, suspending until the lock is free; fails `concurrency.poisoned` if a holder was terminated by a defect (unreachable on the interpreter, where a defect ends the program) |
| `trusted try func lockBlocking(self) MutexGuard[T] from self` | fail, block | an exclusive guard over the value, released when the guard is dropped, blocking the thread until free (the `block` effect); fails `concurrency.poisoned` |

### `class MutexGuard[T]`

| Declaration | Effects | Contract |
|---|---|---|
| `trusted pure func get(self) T where T implements Copyable` | pure; alloc | a copy of the protected value, read through the exclusive guard (12.7); allocates when the value owns heap storage |
| `trusted func set(self, value: owned T)` | mutate | replaces the protected value with value and drops the old one; a write to storage shared between tasks (`mutate`, 11.1) |
| `trusted func replace(self, value: owned T) T` | mutate | replaces the protected value with value and returns the old one, which the caller now owns; a write to storage shared between tasks (`mutate`, 11.1) |

## `fortis.collections`

Collection algorithms (LR 6.7).

### `class Deque[T] implements Iterable[T, ListCursor[T]]`

`front` holds the items from the front end, the first item last, so popping the front is its `pop`; `back` holds the
rest, the last item last. An end that runs dry takes half of the other end's items over, which costs as many moves as
the pushes that filled that end, so both ends are amortised O(1) and no item is copied.

| Declaration | Effects | Contract |
|---|---|---|
| `pure func default() Deque[T]` | pure | an empty deque; O(1) |
| `pure func fromList(items: owned List[T]) Deque[T]` | pure | a deque of the items of the list in order, the first at the front, taking the list's storage; O(1) |
| `pure func count(self) Int` | pure | the number of items; O(1) |
| `pure func isEmpty(self) Bool` | pure | whether the deque holds no item; O(1) |
| `func pushBack(editable self, item: owned T)` | alloc, writes self | adds item after the last one; amortised O(1) |
| `func pushFront(editable self, item: owned T)` | alloc, writes self | adds item before the first one; amortised O(1) |
| `func popFront(editable self) T?` | alloc, writes self | removes and returns the first item, null when empty; amortised O(1), worst case O(count) for the rebalance |
| `func popBack(editable self) T?` | alloc, writes self | removes and returns the last item, null when empty; amortised O(1), worst case O(count) for the rebalance |
| `pure func get(self, index: Int) (alias T from self)?` | pure | a read loan of the item at index, counted from the front, null outside [0, count); O(1) |
| `pure func peekFront(self) (alias T from self)?` | pure | a read loan of the first item, null when empty; O(1) |
| `pure func peekBack(self) (alias T from self)?` | pure | a read loan of the last item, null when empty; O(1) |
| `trusted pure func iterate(self) ListCursor[T] from self` | pure | a cursor over read loans of the items from the front to the back, the items of `front` last to first and then those of `back`; the cursor lists them when it is made, O(count), and each step is O(1) |
| `func each(self, visit: editable fn mut(T) Void)` | none | calls visit with a read loan of every item from the front to the back; the callback may have effects, so `each` is not pure; O(n) plus the callback per item |
| `try func tryEach(self, visit: editable fn mut(T) Outcome[Void])` | fail | as `each`, stopping at the first failure of the callback and returning it; O(n) plus the callback per item |
| `pure func map[U](self, f: pure fn(T) U) Deque[U]` | pure; alloc | a deque of the results of f for every item, in order; allocates; O(n) plus the callback per item |
| `pure try func tryMap[U](self, f: pure fn(T) Outcome[U]) Deque[U]` | pure; alloc, fail | as `map`, stopping at the first failure of the callback and returning it, with the new deque dropped; allocates; O(n) plus the callback per item |
| `pure func filter(self, keep: pure fn(T) Bool) Deque[T] where T implements Copyable` | pure; alloc | a deque of copies of the items keep is true for, in order; allocates; O(n) plus the callback per item |
| `pure func fold[A](self, initial: owned A, step: pure fn(A, T) A) A` | pure | step gets a read loan of the accumulator and an item, once per item from the front to the back, and returns the next accumulator; O(n) plus the callback per item |
| `pure try func tryFold[A](self, initial: owned A, step: pure fn(A, T) Outcome[A]) A` | pure; fail | as `fold`, stopping at the first failure of step and returning it; O(n) plus the callback per item |
| `pure func any(self, holds: pure fn(T) Bool) Bool` | pure | whether holds is true for some item; stops at the first one that passes; O(n) plus the callback |
| `pure func all(self, holds: pure fn(T) Bool) Bool` | pure | whether holds is true for every item; stops at the first one that fails; O(n) plus the callback |
| `pure func find(self, holds: pure fn(T) Bool) (alias T from self)?` | pure | a read loan of the first item holds is true for, null when none does; O(n) plus the callback |
| `pure func indexWhere(self, holds: pure fn(T) Bool) Int?` | pure | the position, counted from the front, of the first item holds is true for, null when none does; O(n) plus the callback |
| `pure func contains(self, target: T) Bool where T implements Equatable` | pure | whether some item equals target; O(n) |
| `pure func toList(self) List[T] where T implements Copyable` | pure; alloc | a list of copies of the items from the front to the back; allocates; O(n) |

### `class SortedSet[T] implements Iterable[T, ListCursor[T]]`

`items` holds the members in ascending order, each once, so a lookup is a binary search over `get`, O(log n). Making
room for a member or closing the gap a removal leaves moves the members after it, one pop and one push each, so `add`
and `remove` are O(n) in the members after the one added or removed; the set operations merge two ascending lists in
one pass, O(n + m).

| Declaration | Effects | Contract |
|---|---|---|
| `pure func default() SortedSet[T] where T implements Comparable` | pure | an empty set; O(1) |
| `pure func fromList(items: owned List[T]) SortedSet[T] where T implements Comparable` | pure; alloc | a set of the items of the list, each once; the list's duplicates are dropped; O(n) times the members each add moves |
| `pure func count(self) Int` | pure | the number of members; O(1) |
| `pure func isEmpty(self) Bool` | pure | whether the set has no member; O(1) |
| `func add(editable self, item: owned T) Bool where T implements Comparable` | alloc, writes self | adds item, true when it was absent; O(log n) to find its place and O(n) in the members after it to make room |
| `pure func contains(self, item: T) Bool where T implements Comparable` | pure | whether item is a member; O(log n) |
| `func remove(editable self, item: T) Bool where T implements Comparable` | alloc, writes self | removes item, true when it was a member; O(log n) to find it and O(n) in the members after it to close the gap |
| `pure func first(self) (alias T from self)?` | pure | a read loan of the smallest member, null when empty; O(1) |
| `pure func last(self) (alias T from self)?` | pure | a read loan of the largest member, null when empty; O(1) |
| `pure func get(self, index: Int) (alias T from self)?` | pure | a read loan of the member at index in ascending order, null outside [0, count); O(1) |
| `pure func iterate(self) ListCursor[T] from self` | pure | the cursor of the sorted list, so a `for` visits the members from the smallest to the largest; O(1) to make, O(1) per step |
| `func each(self, visit: editable fn mut(T) Void)` | none | calls visit with a read loan of every member in ascending order; the callback may have effects, so `each` is not pure; O(n) plus the callback per member |
| `pure func fold[A](self, initial: owned A, step: pure fn(A, T) A) A` | pure | step gets a read loan of the accumulator and a member, once per member in ascending order, and returns the next accumulator; O(n) plus the callback per member |
| `pure func any(self, holds: pure fn(T) Bool) Bool` | pure | whether holds is true for some member; stops at the first one that passes; O(n) plus the callback |
| `pure func all(self, holds: pure fn(T) Bool) Bool` | pure | whether holds is true for every member; stops at the first one that fails; O(n) plus the callback |
| `pure func find(self, holds: pure fn(T) Bool) (alias T from self)?` | pure | a read loan of the smallest member holds is true for, null when none does; O(n) plus the callback |
| `pure func toList(self) List[T] where T implements Copyable` | pure; alloc | a list of copies of the members in ascending order; allocates; O(n) |
| `pure func between(self, low: T, high: T) List[T] where T implements Comparable, T implements Copyable` | pure; alloc | a list of copies of the members from low up to, but not including, high, in ascending order; empty when high is not above low; allocates; O(log n) to find low and O(k) for the k members copied |
| `pure func union(self, other: SortedSet[T]) SortedSet[T] where T implements Comparable, T implements Copyable` | pure; alloc | copies of the members of self and of other, each once, in ascending order; allocates; O(n + m) |
| `pure func intersection(self, other: SortedSet[T]) SortedSet[T] where T implements Comparable, T implements Copyable` | pure; alloc | copies of the members both self and other hold, in ascending order; allocates; O(n + m) |
| `pure func difference(self, other: SortedSet[T]) SortedSet[T] where T implements Comparable, T implements Copyable` | pure; alloc | copies of the members of self that other lacks, in ascending order; allocates; O(n + m) |

### Functions and aspects

| Declaration | Effects | Contract |
|---|---|---|
| `pure func sorted(items: ListView[Int]) List[Int]` | pure | Bottom-up merge sort: stable, O(n log n) comparisons and copies, O(n) extra space. |

### `class FileSystem implements Authority`

| Declaration | Effects | Contract |

| `trusted try func readText(self, path: Path) String` | alloc, fail, block, io | the UTF-8 contents of path below this root; fails `fs.outside_root` when the path is absolute or escapes the root, `fs.not_found`, `fs.not_a_file` or `fs.invalid_text`. | `trusted try func writeAll(self, path: Path, text: StringView)` | alloc, fail, block, io | replaces the contents of path with text, creating the file; fails `fs.outside_root` or `fs.not_found` (missing parent directory); blocks the calling thread (the `block` effect, 11.1) |

# Working with Fortis code

Fortis source is read through the language's tools, never through text tools. `fortis view` sees the code as the
compiler does: it knows which `{` opens a body, which word is a keyword used as a name, and where a statement ends.
`grep` and `cat` do not, and they miss what matters in Fortis (parameter modes, effects, failure disposition).

## Read: `fortis view`

Run from the repository root (`bin/fortis`, or `fortis` when installed). It never writes.

| To | Run |
|---|---|
| read a file, a directory or a glob | `fortis view src/orders.ft`, `fortis view src`, `fortis view 'src/**/*.ft'` |
| list declarations (kind, name, modifiers, contracts, aspects, documentation, head) | `fortis view --decls src` |
| read one declaration whole | `fortis view --symbol process src` or `--symbol Order.total` |
| answer a structural question | `fortis view --query async-try src` |
| list the queries | `fortis view --queries` |

The queries answer what text search cannot: `async`, `try`, `async-try`, `pure`, `noalloc`, `trusted`,
`recovers`, `editable-params`, `owned-params`, `or-fail`, `or-recover`, `catch`, `fail`, `return`, `defer`,
`scope`, `capture`, `expect`, `move`, `lambda`, `tests`, `errors`, `classes`, and `aspect:NAME` (`aspect:get` finds
every `@get` route). Each answer is `file:line:column: name`.

Add `--json` for machine-readable output: one JSON object per line, with `kind` one of `line`, `declaration`,
`symbol`, `match` or `query`. JSON is the primary form, and the terminal highlighting is derived from it.

## Check: `fortis check --format json`

`fortis check FILE.ft` or `fortis check DIR` runs every static check: syntax, names, types, ownership,
obligations, effects, contracts and aspects. With `--format json`, each finding is one record per line. A record
has `code` (for example `E-OWN-001`, LR 7.5), `class`, `rule` (the Language Reference rule it enforces), `file`, `line`,
`column`, `message`, `status` (`violated`, `unproved` or `unknown`) and class-specific `fields`; the schema is
`reference/schemas/diagnostic.schema.json`. A record with a `correction` carries the exact edit that fixes it.
Read the record before changing code: `unproved` means the checker could not prove a refinement, not that the
code is wrong. Run `fortis test FILE.ft` or `fortis test DIR` for the tests.

## Format: `fortis fmt`

`fortis fmt --check PATH` lists the files whose layout is not canonical, and `fortis fmt --write PATH` fixes them.
Formatting changes only whitespace: it refuses, and writes nothing, if a result would not be the same program.

## Rules, codes and corrections: the agent mode

The documentation's agent mode, `docs/agent/` (start at `docs/agent/README.md`), states every rule of the Language
Reference by ID, one page per section, with the diagnostic codes of that section and a rejected-then-accepted
pair of programs for each correction. Every example there is checked and run by the real toolchain.

| To | Read |
|---|---|
| fix a record | `docs/agent/codes.md`: the code's class, rule, Language Reference section, trigger and correction, with a link to its correction pair |
| read a record's fields | `docs/agent/records.md`: the diagnostic record and every runtime record (failures, tests, observation, builds) |
| know the rules of a construct | `docs/agent/NN-*.md`: the rules of Language Reference section NN by ID |
| check a rule's exact words | `docs/Fortis_Language_Reference.md`, the source of truth: `LR 7.3` is its section 7.3 |

A correction pattern shows the smallest change that satisfies the rule. Apply the one whose trigger matches the
record's `code` and `fields`; when the record has a `correction`, apply that edit. Never apply a pattern that
weakens a claim (`pure`, `noalloc`, a contract) or discards an outcome to silence a record.

## Prohibitions

- Do not read `.ft` files with `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `sed -n` or `less`, and do not search them with `grep` or
  `rg`. Use `fortis view`.
- Do not weaken a contract, remove an `expect`, or change an expected output to make a check or test pass.
- Do not hand-format Fortis code; run `fortis fmt --write`.
